title.raw: 卷五十一 列傳第十一 宗室 Volume 51 Biographies 11: Zong Shi

sentences.zh: 列傳第十一 宗室

translations.literal: Biographies 11: Imperial Clan
translations.idiomatic: Biography 11: Members of the Imperial House

sentences.zh: 長沙景王道憐 臨川烈武王道規 營浦侯遵考

translations.literal: Prince Jing of Changsha, Xiao Daolian; Prince Lie Wu of Linchuan, Xiao Daogui; Marquis Zunkao of Yingpu
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daolian, Prince Jing of Changsha; Xiao Daogui, Prince Lie Wu of Linchuan; and Marquis Zunkao of Yingpu

sentences.zh: 長沙景王道憐，高祖中弟也。

translations.literal: Prince Jing of Changsha, Xiao Daolian, was the Gaozu's younger brother born to the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daolian, Prince Jing of Changsha, was a full younger brother of the Founder.

sentences.zh: 初為國子學生。

translations.literal: At first he was a student in the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a student at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 謝琰為徐州，命為從事史。

translations.literal: When Xie Yan was governor of Xuzhou, he appointed him Attendant of the Staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Yan held Xuzhou, he named Daolian a staff attendant.

sentences.zh: 高祖克京城，進平京邑，道憐常留家侍慰太后。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu took the capital region and advanced to pacify the metropolitan city, Daolian constantly remained at home to attend and comfort the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: While the Gaozu seized the capital and marched to pacify the metropolitan region, Daolian usually stayed behind to wait on and comfort the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 桓玄走，大將軍武陵王遵承制，除員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan fled, the Grand General, the Prince of Wuling, Zun, exercised power on imperial commission and appointed him Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Xuan's flight, Grand General Sima Zun, Prince of Wuling, acting on interim authority, named him Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尋遷建威將軍、南彭城內史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Nan Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to General Who Establishes Might and made administrator of Nan Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 時北青州刺史劉該反，引索虜為援，清河、陽平二郡太守孫全聚眾應之。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Gai, Inspector of Northern Qingzhou, rebelled, called in the Northern Wei as allies, and Sun Quan, Administrator of the two commanderies of Qinghe and Yangping, gathered troops in response.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Gai, inspector of Northern Qingzhou, rose in revolt, enlisted Northern Wei support, and Sun Quan, administrator of Qinghe and Yangping, raised forces to join him.

sentences.zh: 義熙元年，索虜托跋開遣偽豫州刺史索度真、大將軍斛斯蘭寇徐州，攻相縣，執鉅鹿太守賀申，進圍寧朔將軍羊穆之於彭城；

translations.literal: In the first year of Yixi, the Northern Wei ruler Tuoba Kai sent the false Inspector of Yuzhou Suo Duzhen and Grand General Husilan to raid Xuzhou, attacked Xiang County, seized He Shen, Administrator of Julu, and advanced to besiege General Who Pacifies the North Yang Muzhi at Pengcheng;
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 1 the Northern Wei ruler Tuoba Kai sent the puppet inspector of Yuzhou Suo Duzhen and Grand General Husilan against Xuzhou; they took Xiang County, captured Julu administrator He Shen, and pressed on to besiege General Who Pacifies the North Yang Muzhi at Pengcheng;

sentences.zh: 穆之告急，道憐率眾救之。

translations.literal: Muzhi reported in emergency; Daolian led troops to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi sent an urgent appeal, and Daolian marched to his relief.

sentences.zh: 軍次陵柵，斬全。

translations.literal: The army halted at Lingzha and beheaded Quan.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Lingzha and beheaded Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 進至彭城，真、蘭退走。

translations.literal: Advancing to Pengcheng, Duzhen and Husilan withdrew and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Pengcheng, Duzhen and Husilan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 道憐率寧遠將軍孟龍符、龍驤將軍孔隆及穆之等追，真、蘭走奔相城；

translations.literal: Daolian led General Who Pacifies the Distant Meng Longfu, General of the Dragon Cavalry Kong Long, Muzhi, and others in pursuit; Duzhen and Husilan fled to Xiangcheng;
translations.idiomatic: Daolian pursued with General Who Pacifies the Distant Meng Longfu, General of the Dragon Cavalry Kong Long, Yang Muzhi, and the rest; Duzhen and Husilan fled to Xiangcheng;

sentences.zh: 又追躡至光水溝，斬劉該，虜眾見殺及赴水死略盡。

translations.literal: Pursuing again to Guangshui Ditch, they beheaded Liu Gai; of the barbarian troops those seen killed and those who drowned in the water were nearly all gone.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on to Guangshui Ditch, slew Liu Gai, and killed or drowned nearly the entire enemy force.

sentences.zh: 高祖鎮京口，進道憐號龍驤將軍，又領堂邑太守，戍石頭。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu garrisoned Jingkou, he advanced Daolian's title to General of the Dragon Cavalry, and he also held the post of Administrator of Tangyi, garrisoning Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaozu took up his post at Jingkou, he promoted Daolian to General of the Dragon Cavalry, gave him Tangyi as well, and stationed him at Shitou.

sentences.zh: 明年，加使持節、監征蜀諸軍事，率冠軍將軍劉敬宣等伐譙縱，而文處茂、溫祚據險不得進，故不果行。

translations.literal: The next year he was given the credential staff and supervision of all military affairs for the campaign against Shu, and led Champion General Liu Jingxuan and others to attack Qiao Zong; but Wen Chumao and Wen Zuo held the passes and he could not advance, so the campaign did not take place.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he received the credential staff and oversight of the Shu expedition and led Champion General Liu Jingxuan and others against Qiao Zong, but Wen Chumao and Wen Zuo held the defiles and blocked his advance, so the campaign was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 以義勳封新興縣五等侯。

translations.literal: For merit in the righteous cause he was enfeoffed as Fifth-Rank Marquis of Xinxing County.
translations.idiomatic: For service in the founding cause he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank marquis of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 四年，代諸葛長民為并州刺史、義昌太守，將軍、內史如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he replaced Zhuge Changmin as Inspector of Bingzhou and Administrator of Yichang; his generalship and interior stewardship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he succeeded Zhuge Changmin as inspector of Bingzhou and administrator of Yichang while keeping his general's title and interior post.

sentences.zh: 猶戍石頭。

translations.literal: He still garrisoned Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: He continued to hold Shitou.

sentences.zh: 時鮮卑侵逼，自彭城以南，民皆保聚，山陽、淮陰諸戍，並不復立。

translations.literal: At that time the Xianbei pressed in; south of Pengcheng the people all gathered in fortified clusters, and the garrisons at Shanyang, Huaiyin, and elsewhere were not re-established.
translations.idiomatic: With the Xianbei pressing in, the people south of Pengcheng clustered in fortified settlements, and the garrisons at Shanyang, Huaiyin, and elsewhere were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 道憐請據彭城，以漸脩創，朝議以彭城縣遠，使鎮山陽。

translations.literal: Daolian requested to hold Pengcheng and gradually restore and build it up; court deliberation held that Pengcheng was too far from the county seat, and he was ordered to garrison Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Daolian asked to hold Pengcheng and rebuild it step by step, but the court judged Pengcheng too remote and stationed him at Shanyang instead.

sentences.zh: 進號征虜將軍、督淮北軍郡事、北東海太守，并州刺史、義昌太守如故。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Captures Barbarians, with supervision of military affairs in the commanderies north of the Huai and the post of Administrator of Northern Donghai; Inspector of Bingzhou and Administrator of Yichang remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Captures Barbarians, given oversight of the Huai-north commanderies and the post of administrator of Northern Donghai, and kept Bingzhou and Yichang.

sentences.zh: 以破索度真功，封新渝縣男，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For the merit of defeating Suo Duzhen he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xinyu County with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For defeating Suo Duzhen he was enfeoffed as baron of Xinyu with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 從高祖征廣固，常為軍鋒。

translations.literal: Following the Gaozu in the campaign against Guanggu, he constantly served as the army's vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the Gaozu's campaign against Guanggu he often led the van.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，慕容超將親兵突圍走，道憐所部獲之。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Murong Chao led his personal troops in a breakout and fled; Daolian's command captured him.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell Murong Chao broke out with his bodyguard, but Daolian's troops seized him.

sentences.zh: 加使持節，進號左將軍。

translations.literal: He was given the credential staff and his title was advanced to General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He received the credential staff and was promoted to General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 七年，解并州，加北徐州刺史，移鎮彭城。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was relieved of Bingzhou, given Northern Xuzhou as well, and transferred his garrison to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he relinquished Bingzhou, added Northern Xuzhou, and moved his headquarters to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 八年，高祖伐劉毅，徵為都督兗、青二州、晉陵、京口、淮南諸郡軍事、兗、青州刺史，持節、將軍、太守如故，還鎮京口。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when the Gaozu attacked Liu Yi, he was summoned as Commander over military affairs in Yan and Qing provinces and the commanderies of Jinling, Jingkou, and Huainan, and as Inspector of Yan and Qing; his credential staff, generalship, and administrator posts remained as before, and he returned to garrison Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when the Gaozu marched against Liu Yi, he was recalled as commander of Yan and Qing and of Jinling, Jingkou, and Huainan, with his staff, general's rank, and posts unchanged, and returned to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 九年，甲仗五十人入殿。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, fifty armed attendants were permitted to enter the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was allowed fifty armed attendants in the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 以廣固功，改封竟陵縣公，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: For merit at Guanggu his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Jingling County with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For the Guanggu campaign he was re-enfeoffed as duke of Jingling with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 減先封戶邑之半，以賜次子義宗。

translations.literal: Half of his earlier enfeoffed households was reduced and granted to his second son Yizong.
translations.idiomatic: Half of his earlier fief was set aside for his second son Yizong.

sentences.zh: 十年，進號中軍將軍，加散騎常侍，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In the tenth year his title was advanced to General of the Central Army; he was given the additional post of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and granted one set of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was promoted to General of the Central Army, made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and granted a full band of martial pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 明年，討司馬休之，道憐監留府事，甲仗百人入殿。

translations.literal: The next year, in the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi, Daolian supervised affairs left at the capital; one hundred armed attendants were permitted to enter the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, while the court campaigned against Sima Xiuzhi, Daolian oversaw the capital in its absence and was allowed one hundred armed attendants in the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 江陵平，以為都督荊、湘、益、秦、寧、梁、雍七州諸軍事、驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司、鎮護南蠻校尉、荊州刺史，持節，常侍如故。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified, he was made Commander over military affairs in the seven provinces of Jing, Xiang, Yi, Qin, Ning, Liang, and Yong, General of Agile Cavalry, with the Grand Marshal's Banners and Three Excellencies' Rites, Colonel Protecting the Southern Man, and Inspector of Jingzhou, with the credential staff; his regular attendant post remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangling fell he was named commander of Jing, Xiang, Yi, Qin, Ning, Liang, and Yong, General of Agile Cavalry with Grand Marshal's Banners and Three Excellencies' Rites, Colonel Protecting the Southern Man, and inspector of Jingzhou, keeping his credential staff and regular attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 北府文武悉配之。

translations.literal: All civil and military officials of the Northern Headquarters were assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: The entire Northern Headquarters staff was assigned to his command.

sentences.zh: 道憐素無才能，言音甚楚，舉止施為，多諸鄙拙。

translations.literal: Daolian had always lacked ability; his speech was very Chu in accent, and his conduct and actions were mostly crude and awkward.
translations.idiomatic: Daolian had never shown talent; he spoke with a heavy Chu accent, and his bearing and habits were mostly coarse and awkward.

sentences.zh: 高祖雖遣將軍佐輔之，而貪縱過甚，畜聚財貨，常若不足，去鎮之日，府庫為之空虛。

translations.literal: Although the Gaozu sent generals to assist him, his greed and license were excessive; he hoarded wealth and goods as though never having enough, and on the day he left his post the treasury was emptied on his account.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Gaozu sent generals to assist him, his greed and excess knew no bounds; he amassed wealth as if he could never have enough, and when he left his post the regional treasury stood empty.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉九年，詔曰：「古者明王經國，司勳有典，平章以馭德刑，班瑞以疇功烈，銘徽庸於鼎彝，配祫祀於清廟。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanjia under the Taizu, an edict said: "In antiquity enlightened kings governed the state; the Director of Merit had his statutes, assessed merit to govern virtue and punishment, distributed jade regalia to rank achievements, inscribed fine merit on tripods and bells, and paired them in joint offerings at the Pure Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yuanjia the Taizu issued an edict: "In antiquity enlightened kings ordered the realm: the Director of Merit kept the statutes, weighed merit to govern virtue and punishment, bestowed jade regalia to rank achievements, engraved worthy deeds on tripods and bells, and granted them joint sacrifice in the Pure Temple.

sentences.zh: 是以從饗先王，義存商誥，祭於大蒸，禮著周典。

translations.literal: Thus they shared in feasting the former kings; the meaning survives in the Announcement of Shang; sacrifice at the Great Offering is ritual made plain in the Zhou canon.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they shared the feast of former kings, as the meaning survives in the Announcement of Shang; the Great Offering sacrifice is ritual set forth in the Zhou canon.

sentences.zh: 自漢迄晉，世崇其文，王猷既昭，幽顯咸秩。

translations.literal: From Han through Jin, the age honored this pattern; once the royal design was made clear, the hidden and manifest alike were set in order.
translations.idiomatic: From Han through Jin each age honored this pattern; when the royal design was made clear, the seen and unseen alike were set in order.

sentences.zh: 先皇經緯天地，撥亂受終，駿命爰集，光宅區宇。

translations.literal: The late emperor wove heaven and earth, quelled disorder and received the mandate's end; the great charge gathered upon him, and his radiance filled the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor ordered heaven and earth, quelled disorder and received the mandate; the great charge gathered on him, and his radiance filled the realm.

sentences.zh: 雖聖明淵運，三靈允協，抑亦股肱翼亮之勤，祈父宣力之效。

translations.literal: Although his sagely clarity was profound in its working and the three numina truly accorded, it was also the diligence of arms and flanks that aided and brightened, the effect of the Prayer-Master's proclaiming of strength.
translations.idiomatic: Though his sagely clarity worked in the depths and the three numina truly accorded, it was also the diligence of his chief ministers and the loyal service of those who bore the burden of rule.

sentences.zh: 故使持節、侍中、都督南徐、兗二州、揚州之晉陵、京口諸軍事、太傅、南徐、兗二州刺史長沙景王，故侍中、大司馬臨川烈武王，故司徒南康文宣公穆之，侍中、衛將軍、開府儀同三司、錄尚書事、揚州刺史華容縣開國公弘，使持節、散騎常侍、都督江州、豫州、西陽、新蔡、晉熙四郡軍事、征南大將軍、開府儀同三司、江州刺史永脩縣開國公道濟，故左將軍、青州刺史龍陽縣開國侯鎮惡，或履道廣流，秉德沖邈，或雅量高劭，風鑒明遠，或識唯知正，才略開邁，咸文德以熙帝載，武功以隆景業，固以侔蹤姬旦，方軌伊、邵者矣。

translations.literal: Thus the late Prince Jing of Changsha, credential staff, Palace Attendant, Commander over military affairs in Southern Xu and Yan provinces and Jinling and Jingkou in Yangzhou, Grand Tutor, and Inspector of Southern Xu and Yan; the late Palace Attendant and Grand Marshal, Prince Lie Wu of Linchuan; the late Minister of Works, Duke Wenxuan of Nangang, Muzhi; Palace Attendant, General of the Guards, with Grand Marshal's Banners and Three Excellencies' Rites, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Inspector of Yangzhou, the founding Duke of Huarong, Hong; credential staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander over military affairs in Jiang, Yu, and the four commanderies of Xiyang, Xincai, and Jinxi, General Who Conquers the South, with Grand Marshal's Banners and Three Excellencies' Rites, and Inspector of Jiangzhou, the founding Duke of Yongxiu, Daoji; and the late General of the Left and Inspector of Qingzhou, the founding Marquis of Longyang, Zhen'e—some treading the Way in broad flow, holding virtue serene and remote; some of lofty measure and stern excellence, wind and mirror bright and far; some in insight knowing only the upright, in talent and strategy opening and advancing—all by civil virtue illumined the imperial carriage and by martial achievement raised the glorious enterprise, truly matching the tracks of the Duke of Zhou and running level with Yi Yin and Duke Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the late Prince Jing of Changsha; the late Prince Lie Wu of Linchuan, grand marshal; the late Duke Wenxuan of Nangang, Muzhi; the founding Duke of Huarong, Hong, who recorded the affairs of state as inspector of Yangzhou; the founding Duke of Yongxiu, Daoji, who conquered the south as inspector of Jiangzhou; and the late Marquis of Longyang, Zhen'e—some walked the Way in breadth and held virtue serene; some bore lofty measure and clear judgment; some knew only the upright path and opened bold designs—all by civil virtue lit the imperial age and by martial achievement raised the glorious enterprise, truly matching the Duke of Zhou and running level with Yi Yin and Duke Shao.

sentences.zh: 朕以寡德，纂戎鴻緒，每惟道勳，思遵令典，而大常未銘，從祀尚闕，鑒寐欽屬，永言深懷。

translations.literal: We, of meager virtue, have succeeded to the great enterprise and every day recall their Way and merit, thinking to follow the fine statutes; yet the Court of Sacrifices has not yet inscribed them, and joint sacrifice is still lacking—reflecting whether waking or sleeping, reverently mindful, we speak of this with lasting depth of feeling.
translations.idiomatic: We, of little virtue, have succeeded to the great enterprise and daily recall their service, wishing to follow the fine statutes; yet the Court of Sacrifices has not inscribed them and joint sacrifice is still lacking—waking or sleeping we hold them in reverent mind and long brood on the debt.

sentences.zh: 便宜敬是前式，憲茲嘉禮，勒功天府，配祭廟庭，俾示徽章，垂美長世，茂績遠猷，永傳不朽。」

translations.literal: It is fitting now to revere this former pattern, take this excellent rite as law, inscribe their merit in the Heavenly Repository, and pair them in sacrifice at the temple court, thereby displaying their honored insignia, leaving beauty for long ages—abundant achievement and far-reaching design, transmitted forever without perishing."
translations.idiomatic: Let us therefore honor the former pattern, enact this excellent rite, inscribe their merit in the Heavenly Repository, and grant them joint sacrifice in the temple court, displaying their honored insignia and leaving beauty for ages—abundant achievement and far-reaching design, to be transmitted forever without end."

sentences.zh: 道憐六子：義欣嗣、義慶、義融、義宗、義賓、義綦。

translations.literal: Daolian had six sons: Yixin, who succeeded; Yiqing; Yirong; Yizong; Yibin; and Yiqi.
translations.idiomatic: Daolian had six sons: Yixin, who succeeded him; Yiqing; Yirong; Yizong; Yibin; and Yiqi.

sentences.zh: 于時土境荒毀，人民彫散，城郭頹敗，盜賊公行。

translations.literal: At that time the territory was wasted and ruined, the people scattered and depleted, city walls collapsed and broken, and bandits walked openly.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the land lay waste, the people were scattered and depleted, the walls were in ruins, and bandits roamed openly.

sentences.zh: 義欣綱維補緝，隨宜經理，劫盜所經，立討誅之制。

translations.literal: Yixin drew up the framework, repaired and mended, managed affairs as suited to circumstances, and wherever bandits passed established regulations for pursuit and execution.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin restored order, managed affairs as circumstances required, and wherever bandits struck established rules for pursuit and punishment.

sentences.zh: 境內畏服，道不拾遺，城府庫藏，竝皆完實，遂為盛藩強鎮。

translations.literal: Within the borders all feared and submitted; nothing was left on the roads, and the city treasury stores were all complete and full, so that it became a flourishing great fief and strong garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The region submitted in awe; nothing was left lying on the roads, and the city treasuries stood full, so that his domain became a flourishing great fief and strong garrison.

sentences.zh: 時淮西、江北長吏，悉敘勞人武夫，多無政術。

translations.literal: At that time the chief officials west of the Huai and north of the river were all men promoted for labor service or martial prowess, and most lacked skill in governance.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the chief officials west of the Huai and north of the river were mostly veterans promoted for labor or fighting, with little skill in governance.

sentences.zh: 義欣陳之曰：「江淮左右，土塉民疏，頃年以來，薦饑相襲，百城彫弊，於今為甚。

translations.literal: Yixin memorialized, saying: "To left and right of the Yangzi and Huai the soil is thin and the people sparse; in recent years famine has followed famine, and the hundred cities are wasted—today it is worst of all.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin memorialized: "On both sides of the Yangzi and Huai the soil is poor and the people thin; famine has followed famine in recent years, and the hundred cities are wasted—today the distress is worst of all.

sentences.zh: 綏牧之宜，必俟良吏。

translations.literal: What is fitting for soothing and pasturing must await good officials.
translations.idiomatic: To soothe and govern the people requires able officials.

sentences.zh: 勞人武夫，不經政術，統內官長，多非才授。

translations.literal: Laborers and fighting men, untrained in the arts of government—of the officials within the command, many were not appointed for talent.
translations.idiomatic: Laborers and fighting men untrained in government fill the posts, and most local chiefs were not chosen for ability.

sentences.zh: 東南殷實，猶或簡能，況賓接荒垂，而可輯柔頓闕。

translations.literal: In the prosperous southeast they still sometimes select for ability; how much more at this frontier of desolation—can soothing and gentleness be suddenly lacking?
translations.idiomatic: Even in the prosperous southeast they still choose for ability; how much more on this devastated frontier can we neglect soothing rule?

sentences.zh: 願敕選部，必使任得其人，庶得不勞而治。」

translations.literal: We beg that the Selection Bureau be ordered to ensure that each post gets the right man, so that perhaps rule may be achieved without strain."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the Selection Bureau be ordered to place the right man in each post, so that the region may be governed without undue strain."

sentences.zh: 芍陂良田萬餘頃，堤堨久壞，秋夏常苦旱。

translations.literal: The Quepi had more than ten thousand qing of fine fields; its dikes and embankments had long been ruined, and in autumn and summer drought was constantly a hardship.
translations.idiomatic: The Quepi held more than ten thousand qing of fine farmland; its dikes had long fallen into ruin, and drought plagued every autumn and summer.

sentences.zh: 義欣遣諮議參軍殷肅循行脩理。

translations.literal: Yixin sent Adviser-Consultant Staff Officer Yin Su on a circuit to repair and restore it.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin sent Adviser-Consultant Staff Officer Yin Su to tour the works and restore them.

sentences.zh: 有舊溝引渒水入陂，不治積久，樹木榛塞。

translations.literal: There was an old channel drawing the Fei River into the reservoir; it had not been maintained for long accumulation of time, and trees and brambles blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: An old channel drew the Fei River into the reservoir, but it had long gone unrepaired and was choked with trees and brush.

sentences.zh: 肅伐木開榛，水得通注，旱患由是得除。

translations.literal: Su felled trees and cleared the brambles; water was able to flow through, and the hardship of drought was thereby removed.
translations.idiomatic: Su felled the trees and cleared the brush; the water flowed again, and drought was relieved.

sentences.zh: 十年，進號鎮軍將軍，進監為都督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year his title was advanced to General Who Guards the Army, and his supervisory post was advanced to Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was promoted to General Who Guards the Army and his supervisory post to full commander.

sentences.zh: 十一年夏，入朝，太祖厚加恩禮。

translations.literal: In the summer of the eleventh year he entered court; the Taizu greatly increased his favor and ritual honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the eleventh year he came to court, and the Taizu heaped favor and ceremony on him.

sentences.zh: 十六年，薨，時年三十六。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died; he was thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he died at the age of thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 追贈散騎常侍、征西將軍、開府儀同三司，持節、都督、刺史如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Conquers the West, and Grand Marshal's Banners and Three Excellencies' Rites; his credential staff, command, and inspector posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General Who Conquers the West with Grand Marshal's Banners and Three Excellencies' Rites, keeping his staff, command, and inspector titles.

sentences.zh: 諡曰成王。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Prince Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Prince Cheng.

sentences.zh: 瑾弟祗，字彥期，大明中為中書郎。

translations.literal: Jin's younger brother Zhi, courtesy name Yanqi, in the Daming era was a Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's younger brother Zhi, styled Yanqi, served as Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat in the Daming era.

sentences.zh: 太宰江夏王義恭領中書監，服親不得相臨，表求解職。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor, the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, held the post of Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat; as kin within mourning they could not face each other in office, and he memorialized requesting to be relieved of his post.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, held the supervisor's post at the Palace Secretariat; as close kin in mourning they could not serve together, and Zhi memorialized to resign.

sentences.zh: 世祖詔曰：「昔二王兩謝，俱至崇禮，自今三臺五省，悉同此例。」

translations.literal: The Shizu issued an edict: "In the past the two Wangs and the two Xies all received honored ritual; from now on the Three Platforms and Five Ministries shall all follow this precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu decreed: "In the past the two Wangs and the two Xies all received honored ritual; from now on the Three Platforms and Five Ministries shall follow this precedent."

sentences.zh: 太宗初，為南兗州刺史、都官尚書，謀應晉安王子勛為逆，伏誅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taizong's reign he was Inspector of Southern Yanzhou and Minister of Justice; he plotted to join Jin'an Prince Zixun's rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he was inspector of Southern Yanzhou and Minister of Justice; he plotted to join Prince Zixun of Jin'an's rebellion and was executed.

sentences.zh: 韞弟弼，武昌太守，亦與子勛同逆，伏誅。

translations.literal: Yun's younger brother Bi, Administrator of Wuchang, also joined Zixun's rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's younger brother Bi, administrator of Wuchang, also joined Zixun's rebellion and was executed.

sentences.zh: 弟鑒，員外散騎侍郎，蚤卒。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jian was Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jian was Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and died young.

sentences.zh: 監弟勰，字彥和，侍中，吳興太守，後廢帝元徽元年卒。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brother Xie, courtesy name Yanhe, was Palace Attendant and Administrator of Wuxing; he died in the first year of Yuanhui under the Deposed Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Xie, styled Yanhe, was palace attendant and administrator of Wuxing; he died in Yuanhui 1 under the Deposed Emperor.

sentences.zh: 勰弟顥，字彥明，侍中、左衛將軍，冠軍將軍、吳興太守，未拜，元徽四年卒，追贈右將軍。

translations.literal: Xie's younger brother Hao, courtesy name Yanming, was Palace Attendant and General of the Left Guard, and was appointed Champion General and Administrator of Wuxing but did not assume the post; he died in the fourth year of Yuanhui and was posthumously given General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Xie's younger brother Hao, styled Yanming, was palace attendant and General of the Left Guard and was named champion general and administrator of Wuxing but never took up the post; he died in Yuanhui 4 and was posthumously made General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 顥弟述，東陽太守，黃門郎，與從弟秉同逆，事敗，走白山，追禽伏誅。

translations.literal: Hao's younger brother Shu was Administrator of Dongyang and a Gentleman at the Yellow Gate; with his cousin Bing he joined the rebellion; when the affair failed he fled to Baishan, was pursued and captured, and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's younger brother Shu was administrator of Dongyang and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate; with his cousin Bing he rebelled, and when the plot failed he fled to Baishan, was captured, and executed.

sentences.zh: 義欣弟義慶，出繼臨川烈武王道規。

translations.literal: Yixin's younger brother Yiqing was given in adoption to succeed Prince Lie Wu of Linchuan, Daogui.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin's younger brother Yiqing was adopted to succeed Prince Lie Wu of Linchuan, Daogui.

sentences.zh: 子孝侯顗嗣，官至太子翊軍校尉，為元兇所殺。

translations.literal: His son, Marquis Xiao Yi, succeeded; he reached the post of Colonel of the Heir Apparent's Supporting Army and was killed by the Arch-Culprit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi, Marquis Xiao, succeeded him, rose to Colonel of the Heir Apparent's Supporting Army, and was killed by the Arch-Culprit Liu Shao.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，追贈散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When the Shizu took the throne he was posthumously given Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne he was posthumously made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟襲以子晃繼封。

translations.literal: He had no son; his younger brother Xi let his son Huang succeed to the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son; his younger brother Xi had his son Huang succeed to the fief.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年，與員外散騎侍郎安成戢仁祖、荒人王武連、羽林副彭元儁等謀反，國除。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming he plotted rebellion with Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Ji Renzu of Ancheng, the frontier man Wang Wulian, Forest of Feathers Deputy Peng Yuanjun, and others; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 2 he plotted rebellion with Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant Ji Renzu of Ancheng, the frontier man Wang Wulian, Forest of Feathers Deputy Peng Yuanjun, and others, and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 襲字茂德，太子舍人，安成太守。

translations.literal: Xi, courtesy name Maode, was a Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Administrator of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, styled Maode, was Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent and administrator of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 晉安王子勛為逆，襲據郡距之，子勛遣軍攻圍不能下。

translations.literal: When Jin'an Prince Zixun rebelled, Xi held the commandery and resisted him; Zixun sent troops to attack and besiege but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zixun of Jin'an rebelled, Xi held Ancheng and resisted him; Zixun's troops besieged the city but could not take it.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉之，以為郢州刺史，封建陵縣侯，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: The Taizong commended him and appointed him Inspector of Yingzhou, enfeoffing him as Marquis of Jianling County with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming commended him, named him inspector of Yingzhou, and enfeoffed him as marquis of Jianling with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 建陵縣屬蒼梧郡，以道遠，改封臨澧縣侯。

translations.literal: Jianling County belonged to Cangwu Commandery; because the road was far, his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Linli County.
translations.idiomatic: Jianling lay in Cangwu commandery; because it was too remote, his fief was moved to Linli.

sentences.zh: 始六年，卒於中護軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taishi he died while holding the post of Central Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taishi he died while serving as Central Guard General.

sentences.zh: 追贈護軍將軍，加散騎常侍，諡曰忠侯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given General Who Guards the Army and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; his posthumous title was Marquis Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Guards the Army and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, with the posthumous title Marquis Zhong.

sentences.zh: 襲亦庸鄙，在郢州，暑月露{巾軍}上聽事，綱紀正伏閣，怪之，訪問，乃知是襲。

translations.literal: Xi was also vulgar and crude; in Yingzhou, in the heat of summer he slept in only his drawers in the open in the audience hall; the staff officer was then at his post in the side chamber, found it strange, inquired, and only then learned it was Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was likewise coarse and vulgar; as inspector of Yingzhou, in midsummer he slept in only his drawers in the open audience hall while his staff officer was at his post in the side chamber; puzzled, the officer inquired and learned it was Xi.

sentences.zh: 子旻嗣，昇明三年，改封東昌縣侯，與兄晃俱伏誅。

translations.literal: His son Min succeeded; in the third year of Shengming his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Dongchang County; he and his elder brother Huang were both executed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Min succeeded; in Shengming 3 the fief was moved to Dongchang, and he and his elder brother Huang were both executed.

sentences.zh: 襲弟彪，秘書郎；

translations.literal: Xi's younger brother Biao was a Gentleman of the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Xi's younger brother Biao was Gentleman of the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 弟寔，太子舍人，竝蚤卒。

translations.literal: his younger brother Shi was a Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent; both died young.
translations.idiomatic: his younger brother Shi was Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent; both died young.

sentences.zh: 寔弟爽，海陵太守。

translations.literal: Shi's younger brother Shuang was Administrator of Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's younger brother Shuang was administrator of Hailing.

sentences.zh: 子懷侯玠嗣，琅邪、秦郡太守。

translations.literal: His son, Marquis Huai Jie, succeeded and served as Administrator of Langye and Qin commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jie, Marquis Huai, succeeded him and served as administrator of Langye and Qin.

sentences.zh: 爲元凶所殺，追贈散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was killed by the Arch-Culprit and posthumously given Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed by the Arch-Culprit and posthumously made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟秉以子承繼封。

translations.literal: He had no son; his younger brother Bing let his son Cheng succeed to the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son; his younger brother Bing had his son Cheng succeed to the fief.

sentences.zh: 秉字彥節，初為著作郎，歷羽林監，越騎校尉，中書、黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Bing, courtesy name Yanjie, at first was a Gentleman Author; he passed through the posts of Supervisor of the Forest of Feathers, Colonel of the Upland Cavalry, and Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat and at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Bing, styled Yanjie, began as Gentleman Author and served as Supervisor of the Forest of Feathers, Colonel of the Upland Cavalry, and Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat and at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始初，為侍中，頻徙左衛將軍，丹陽尹，太子詹事，吏部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi under the Taizong he was Palace Attendant and was repeatedly transferred among General of the Left Guard, Governor of Danyang, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taishi under Emperor Ming he was palace attendant and moved repeatedly among General of the Left Guard, governor of Danyang, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時宗室雖多，材能甚寡。

translations.literal: Although the imperial clan was numerous at the time, men of talent were very few.
translations.idiomatic: Though the imperial clan was large, men of real ability were scarce.

sentences.zh: 秉少自砥束，甚得朝野之譽，故為太宗所委。

translations.literal: Bing from youth disciplined himself and won great praise in court and countryside, and therefore was entrusted by the Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Bing had disciplined himself from youth and won wide praise in court and country, and Emperor Ming entrusted him accordingly.

sentences.zh: 五年，出為前將軍、淮南、宣城二郡太守，不拜，還復本任。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was sent out as General of the Vanguard and Administrator of the two commanderies of Huainan and Xuancheng; he did not accept the appointment and returned to his former posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was named General of the Vanguard and administrator of Huainan and Xuancheng but declined and returned to his former posts.

sentences.zh: 復為侍中，守秘書監，領太子詹事。

translations.literal: He again became Palace Attendant, acting Supervisor of the Secretariat, and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He again became palace attendant, acting supervisor of the Secretariat, and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 未拜，遷使持節、都督南徐、徐、兗、豫、青、冀六州諸軍事、後將軍、南徐州刺史，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Before he assumed the post he was transferred to credential staff, Commander over military affairs in the six provinces of Southern Xu, Xu, Yan, Yu, Qing, and Ji, General of the Rear, and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, with the additional post of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post he was transferred to credential staff, commander of Southern Xu, Xu, Yan, Yu, Qing, and Ji, General of the Rear and inspector of Southern Xuzhou, with Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry added.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝即位，改都督郢州、豫州之西陽、司州之義陽二郡諸軍事、郢州刺史，持節、常侍如故。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, his command was changed to military affairs in Yingzhou and the two commanderies of Xiyang in Yuzhou and Yiyang in Sizhou, and Inspector of Yingzhou; his credential staff and regular attendant post remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Bing's command was changed to Yingzhou and the commanderies of Xiyang and Yiyang, with inspector of Yingzhou; he kept his staff and regular attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 未拜，留為尚書左僕射，參選。

translations.literal: Before he assumed the post he was retained as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, participating in selections.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post he was kept at court as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with a role in personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 元徽元年，領吏部，加兵五百人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhui he concurrently held the Ministry of Personnel and was given five hundred additional troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui 1 he took charge of the Ministry of Personnel and was given five hundred additional troops.

sentences.zh: 尋領衛尉，辭不拜。

translations.literal: Soon he was given concurrent charge of the Commandant of the Guards but declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named Commandant of the Guards as well but declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 桂陽王休範為逆，中領軍劉勔出守石頭，秉權兼領軍將軍，所給加兵，自隨入殿。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Guiyang, Xiufan, rebelled, Central Guard General Liu Kan went out to hold Shitou; Bing by authority concurrently held the post of General of the Central Army, and the additional troops granted him entered the palace hall with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled, Central Guard General Liu Kan went to hold Shitou; Bing acted as General of the Central Army in his stead, and his additional troops entered the palace hall with him.

sentences.zh: 二年，加散騎常侍、丹陽尹，解吏部。

translations.literal: In the second year he was given Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Governor of Danyang and was relieved of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and governor of Danyang and relinquished the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 封當陽縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dangyang County with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as marquis of Dangyang with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 與齊王、袁粲、褚淵分日入直決機事。

translations.literal: With the Prince of Qi, Yuan Can, and Chu Yuan he took turns on duty deciding critical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He shared rotating duty with the Prince of Qi, Yuan Can, and Chu Yuan, deciding critical affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷中書令，加撫軍將軍，常侍、尹如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Director of the Palace Secretariat and given General Who Pacifies the Army; his regular attendant post and governorship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became Director of the Palace Secretariat and General Who Pacifies the Army, keeping his regular attendant rank and the governorship of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 順帝即位，轉尚書令、中領軍，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shun took the throne he was transferred to Director of the Department of State Affairs and Central Guard General; his generalship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shun took the throne he became Director of the Department of State Affairs and Central Guard General, keeping his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 時齊王輔政，四海屬心，秉知鼎命有在，密懷異圖。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Qi was regent and all within the seas turned their hearts to him; Bing knew the mandate rested with him and secretly harbored a different design.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi was regent and the realm looked to him; Bing saw that the mandate rested with him and secretly plotted against him.

sentences.zh: 袁粲鎮石頭，不識天命，沈攸之舉兵反，齊王入屯朝堂，粲潛與秉及諸大將黃回等謀欲作亂。

translations.literal: Yuan Can garrisoned Shitou and did not recognize Heaven's mandate; when Shen Youzhi raised troops in rebellion the Prince of Qi entered and encamped in the court hall; Can secretly plotted with Bing and the great generals Huang Hui and others to raise disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can held Shitou and refused to accept Heaven's mandate; when Shen Youzhi rebelled the Prince of Qi took up position in the court hall, and Can secretly plotted with Bing, Huang Hui, and other great generals to raise a revolt.

sentences.zh: 本期夜會石頭，旦乃舉兵。

translations.literal: They had planned to meet at Shitou by night and raise troops at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: They had planned to meet at Shitou by night and rise at dawn.

sentences.zh: 秉素恇怯騷動，擾不自安，再餔後，便自丹陽郡車載婦女，盡室奔石頭，部曲數百，赫弈滿道。

translations.literal: Bing had always been timid, fearful, and restless; unable to settle himself, after the second meal he loaded women into carts from Danyang commandery and fled with his whole household to Shitou; several hundred retainers filled the road in splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Bing had always been timid and restless; after the midday meal he loaded his women into carts from Danyang and fled with his whole household to Shitou, several hundred retainers crowding the road in splendor.

sentences.zh: 既至見粲，粲驚曰：「何遽便來，事今敗矣！」

translations.literal: When he arrived and saw Can, Can said in alarm: "Why have you come so hastily? The affair is ruined!"
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Can, Can cried in alarm: "Why have you come so soon? The plot is ruined!"

sentences.zh: 秉曰：「今得見公，萬死亦何恨。」

translations.literal: Bing said: "Now that I have seen you, sir, what regret is there though I die ten thousand deaths?"
translations.idiomatic: Bing said: "Now that I have seen you, sir, I regret nothing though I die ten thousand deaths."

sentences.zh: 從弟中領軍韞，直在省內，與直閣將軍卜伯興謀，其夜共攻齊王。

translations.literal: His cousin Central Guard General Yun was on duty inside the palace and plotted with Direct-Gate General Bu Boxing; that night they jointly attacked the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Central Guard General Yun, on duty in the palace, plotted with Direct-Gate General Bu Boxing to attack the Prince of Qi that night.

sentences.zh: 會秉去事覺，齊王夜使驍騎將軍王敬則收韞。

translations.literal: When Bing's departure made the affair known, the Prince of Qi at night sent Swift Cavalry General Wang Jingze to seize Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Bing's flight exposed the plot, and the Prince of Qi sent Swift Cavalry General Wang Jingze that night to seize Yun.

sentences.zh: 韞已戒嚴，敬則率壯士直前，韞左右皆披靡，因殺之，伯興亦伏誅。

translations.literal: Yun had already taken up arms; Jingze led stalwarts straight forward, Yun's attendants all scattered, and he was killed; Boxing was also executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yun had already taken up arms; Jingze led his men straight in, Yun's guards scattered, and he was killed; Boxing was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 粲敗，秉踰城出走，於頟檐湖見擒，與二子承、俁並死。

translations.literal: When Can was defeated, Bing climbed over the wall and fled; at Eyan Lake he was captured and died together with his two sons Cheng and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When Can was defeated Bing climbed over the wall and fled; he was captured at Eyan Lake and died with his two sons Cheng and Yu.

sentences.zh: 秉時年四十五。

translations.literal: Bing was then forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Bing was forty-five.

sentences.zh: 秉妻蕭氏，思話女也。

translations.literal: Bing's wife was the Lady Xiao, a daughter of Sihua.
translations.idiomatic: Bing's wife was Lady Xiao, daughter of Sihua.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，朝廷危殆，妻常懼禍敗，每謂秉曰：「君富貴已足，故應為兒子作計。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhui era the court was in peril; his wife constantly feared disaster and ruin and often said to Bing: "Your wealth and honor are already sufficient; you ought therefore to make plans for your sons.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhui era, when the court stood in peril, his wife feared disaster and often told Bing: "You have wealth and honor enough; you ought to plan for your sons.

sentences.zh: 年垂五十，殘生何足吝邪！」

translations.literal: You are nearly fifty—what is there to cherish in a remnant of life!"
translations.idiomatic: You are nearly fifty—what is a remnant of life worth clinging to?"

sentences.zh: 秉不能從。

translations.literal: Bing could not follow her advice.
translations.idiomatic: Bing would not listen.

sentences.zh: 秉弟謨，奉朝請。

translations.literal: Bing's younger brother Mo was a Court Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Bing's younger brother Mo was a court attendant.

sentences.zh: 謨弟遐，字彥道，亦奉朝請、員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Mo's younger brother Xia, courtesy name Yandao, was also a Court Attendant and Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Mo's younger brother Xia, styled Yandao, was also a court attendant and Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 與嫡母殷養女雲敷私通，殷每禁之。

translations.literal: He had a secret affair with Yunfu, the foster daughter of his stepmother Lady Yin; Yin constantly forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: He had a secret affair with Yunfu, his stepmother Lady Yin's foster daughter, whom Lady Yin repeatedly forbade him to see.

sentences.zh: 殷暴病卒，未大殮，口鼻流血，疑遐潛加毒害，為有司所糾。

translations.literal: Yin died suddenly of illness; before the full encoffining blood flowed from her mouth and nose; Xia was suspected of secretly poisoning her and was impeached by the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yin died suddenly; before she was fully encoffined blood flowed from her mouth and nose, and Xia was suspected of poisoning her and impeached by the authorities.

sentences.zh: 世祖徙之始安郡，永光中，得還。

translations.literal: The Shizu exiled him to Shi'an commandery; in the Yongguang era he was allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu exiled him to Shi'an commandery; in the Yongguang era he was allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 太宗世，歷黃門侍郎，都官尚書，吳郡太守。

translations.literal: In the Taizong's reign he passed through the posts of Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, Minister of Justice, and Administrator of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he served as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, Minister of Justice, and administrator of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 兄秉既死，齊王遣誅之。

translations.literal: After his elder brother Bing died, the Prince of Qi sent men to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: After his brother Bing died, the Prince of Qi had him executed.

sentences.zh: 遐人才甚凡，自諱名，常對賓客曰：「孝武無道，枉我殺母。」

translations.literal: Xia's talent was very ordinary; he avoided speaking his name and often said to guests: "Emperor Xiaowu was without the Way and wrongly had me kill my mother."
translations.idiomatic: Xia was thoroughly mediocre; he avoided his own name and often told guests: "Emperor Xiaowu was without the Way and wrongly made me kill my mother."

sentences.zh: 其頑騃若此。

translations.literal: His stupidity was of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: He was as stupid as that.

sentences.zh: 秉當權，遐累求方伯，秉曰：「我在，用汝作州，於聽望不足。」

translations.literal: When Bing held power, Xia repeatedly asked for a regional post; Bing said: "While I am here, to use you as a provincial governor would fall short of what is heard and expected."
translations.idiomatic: While Bing held power, Xia repeatedly asked for a provincial post; Bing said: "While I am in office, making you a provincial governor would damage our family's standing."

sentences.zh: 遐曰：「富貴時則云不可相關，從坐之日，為得免不？」

translations.literal: Xia said: "In times of wealth and honor you say we cannot be connected; on the day of shared guilt, will I be spared or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Xia said: "In good times you say we cannot be connected; when guilt is shared, will I be spared?"

sentences.zh: 至是果死焉。

translations.literal: At this he indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: He was indeed killed.

sentences.zh: 義宗弟義賓，元嘉二年，封新野縣侯。

translations.literal: Yizong's younger brother Yibin, in the second year of Yuanjia, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinye County.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong's younger brother Yibin was enfeoffed as marquis of Xinye in the second year of Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 六年，以新野荒敝，改封興安縣侯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, because Xinye was desolate and impoverished, his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Xing'an County.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, because Xinye was desolate and poor, his fief was moved to Xing'an.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎，秘書監，左衛將軍，位至輔國將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, Supervisor of the Secretariat, and General of the Left Guard, and reached the posts of General Who Supports the State and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, supervisor of the Secretariat, and General of the Left Guard, and rose to General Who Supports the State and inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，卒，追贈後將軍，諡曰肅侯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died; he was posthumously given General of the Rear, and his posthumous title was Marquis Su.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he died and was posthumously made General of the Rear, with the posthumous title Marquis Su.

sentences.zh: 子惠侯綜嗣。

translations.literal: His son, Marquis Hui Zong, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zong, Marquis Hui, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子憲嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian succeeded.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年，齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming Qi received the abdication; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 2 Qi received the abdication and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 綜弟琨，晉平太守。

translations.literal: Zong's younger brother Kun was Administrator of Jinping.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's younger brother Kun was administrator of Jinping.

sentences.zh: 義賓弟義綦，元嘉六年，封營道縣侯。

translations.literal: Yibin's younger brother Yiqi, in the sixth year of Yuanjia, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yingdao County.
translations.idiomatic: Yibin's younger brother Yiqi was enfeoffed as marquis of Yingdao in the sixth year of Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 凡鄙無識知，每為始興王濬兄弟所戲弄。

translations.literal: He was vulgar, crude, and without understanding, and was constantly mocked by the brothers of the Prince of Shixing, Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He was vulgar and ignorant and was constantly mocked by Prince Jun of Shixing and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 濬嘗謂義綦曰：「陸士衡詩云：『營道無烈心。』

translations.literal: Jun once said to Yiqi: "Lu Shiheng's poem says: 'On the road to Yingdao there is no ardent heart.'
translations.idiomatic: Jun once told Yiqi: "Lu Ji wrote in a poem: 'On the road to Yingdao there is no ardent heart.'

sentences.zh: 其何意苦阿父如此？」

translations.literal: What does it mean to torment your honored father so?"
translations.idiomatic: What does it mean to torment your honored father so?"

sentences.zh: 義綦曰：「下官初不識，何忽見苦。」

translations.literal: Yiqi said: "This humble official did not recognize it at first—why am I suddenly tormented?"
translations.idiomatic: Yiqi said: "I never knew that line—why am I suddenly tormented?"

sentences.zh: 其庸塞可笑類若此。

translations.literal: His obtuseness and blockishness were laughably of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His dullness was laughably of this kind.

sentences.zh: 歷右衛將軍，湘州刺史。

translations.literal: He passed through the posts of General of the Right Guard and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as General of the Right Guard and inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年，卒，贈平南將軍，諡曰僖侯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian he died; he was given General Who Pacifies the South, and his posthumous title was Marquis Xi.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 2 he died and was given General Who Pacifies the South, with the posthumous title Marquis Xi.

sentences.zh: 子長猷嗣，官至步兵校尉。

translations.literal: His son Changyou succeeded and reached the post of Colonel of the Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changyou succeeded him and rose to Colonel of the Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 昇平三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengping he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Shengping 3.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 臨川烈武王道規，字道則，高祖少弟也。

translations.literal: Prince Lie Wu of Linchuan, Xiao Daogui, courtesy name Daize, was the Gaozu's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daogui, Prince Lie Wu of Linchuan, styled Daize, was a younger brother of the Founder.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻有大志，高祖奇之，與謀誅桓玄。

translations.literal: In youth he was free-spirited and had great ambition; the Gaozu marveled at him and joined with him in plotting to kill Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was bold and ambitious; the Gaozu admired him and joined him in plotting Huan Xuan's overthrow.

sentences.zh: 時桓弘鎮廣陵，以為征虜中兵參軍。

translations.literal: At that time Huan Hong garrisoned Guangling; he was made a Middle Army Staff Officer under the General Who Captures Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Hong held Guangling, Daogui was made a middle army staff officer under the General Who Captures Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 高祖克京城，道規亦以其日與劉毅、孟昶共斬弘，收眾濟江。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu took the capital region, on that same day Daogui together with Liu Yi and Meng Chang beheaded Hong, gathered the troops, and crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaozu seized the capital, Daogui that same day joined Liu Yi and Meng Chang in beheading Hong, gathered the troops, and crossed the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 進平京邑，玄敗走。

translations.literal: Advancing to pacify the metropolitan city, Xuan was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced to pacify the capital, and Xuan was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 晉大將軍武陵王遵承制，以道規為振武將軍、義昌太守。

translations.literal: Jin Grand General Sima Zun, Prince of Wuling, exercising power on imperial commission, appointed Daogui General Who Quells Martiality and Administrator of Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Sima Zun, Prince of Wuling, acting on interim authority, named Daogui General Who Quells Martiality and administrator of Yichang.

sentences.zh: 與劉毅、何無忌追玄。

translations.literal: With Liu Yi and He Wuji he pursued Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: With Liu Yi and He Wuji he pursued Xuan.

sentences.zh: 玄西走江陵，留郭銓、何澹之等固守盆口，義軍既至，賊列艦距之。

translations.literal: Xuan fled west to Jiangling, leaving Guo Quan, He Tanzhi, and others to hold firm at Penkou; when the righteous army arrived, the rebels lined ships to block them.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan fled west to Jiangling, leaving Guo Quan, He Tanzhi, and others to hold Penkou; when the loyal army arrived, the rebels lined their ships to block the advance.

sentences.zh: 澹之空設羽儀旗幟於一舫，而別在它船，無忌欲攻羽儀所在，眾悉不同，曰：「澹之必不在此舫，雖得無益也。」

translations.literal: Tanzhi had set only ceremonial banners and flags on one ship while he himself was on another; Wuji wanted to attack where the ceremonial display was; all disagreed, saying: "Tanzhi is certainly not on this ship—even if we take it, there is no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhi had placed only ceremonial banners on one ship while he himself was aboard another; Wuji wanted to attack the display ship, but all objected: "Tanzhi is certainly not on that ship—even if we take it, we gain nothing."

sentences.zh: 無忌曰：「澹之不在此舫，固不須言也。

translations.literal: Wuji said: "That Tanzhi is not on this ship goes without saying.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji said: "That Tanzhi is not on that ship goes without saying.

sentences.zh: 既不在此，則戰士必弱，我以勁兵攻之，必可禽也。

translations.literal: Since he is not here, the fighters must be weak; if we attack with crack troops, we can certainly capture it.
translations.idiomatic: Since he is not there, the fighters must be weak; if we attack with crack troops, we can certainly take it.

sentences.zh: 禽之之日，彼必以為失其軍主，我徒咸謂已得賊帥，我勇而彼懼，懼而薄之，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: On the day we capture it, they will surely think they have lost their army commander; our men will all say we have taken the rebel leader—we brave and they afraid; afraid and pressed, they will certainly be broken."
translations.idiomatic: When we take it, they will think they have lost their commander; our men will believe we have seized the rebel leader—we bold and they afraid; afraid and pressed, they will certainly break."

sentences.zh: 道規喜曰：「此名計也。」

translations.literal: Daogui said with delight: "This is a famous stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Daogui said with delight: "That is a famous stratagem."

sentences.zh: 因往彼攻之，即禽此舫。

translations.literal: Thereupon they went and attacked it and at once captured that ship.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked at once and captured the ship.

sentences.zh: 因鼓噪倡曰：「已斬何澹之！」

translations.literal: They then beat drums, shouted, and proclaimed: "He Tanzhi has already been beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: They beat drums, shouted, and proclaimed: "He Tanzhi has been beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 賊徒及義軍竝以為然。

translations.literal: Rebels and righteous army alike believed it.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels and loyal troops alike believed it.

sentences.zh: 因縱兵，賊眾奔敗，即克盆口，進平尋陽。

translations.literal: They then released the troops; the rebel masses fled in defeat; Penkou was taken at once and Xunyang was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed the attack; the rebels broke and fled; Penkou fell at once and Xunyang was pacified.

sentences.zh: 因復馳進，遇玄於崢嶸洲。

translations.literal: They then pressed on again at speed and encountered Xuan at Zhengrong Isle.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on again and met Xuan at Zhengrong Isle.

sentences.zh: 道規等兵不滿萬人，而玄戰士數萬，眾並憚之，欲退還尋陽。

translations.literal: Daogui and the others had fewer than ten thousand men, while Xuan's fighting troops numbered in the tens of thousands; all feared them and wished to withdraw to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui had fewer than ten thousand men while Xuan's forces numbered in the tens of thousands; all feared them and wished to withdraw to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 道規曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Daogui said: "That will not do.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui said: "That will not do.

sentences.zh: 彼眾我寡，強弱異勢。

translations.literal: They are many and we few; strength and weakness differ in circumstance.
translations.idiomatic: They are many and we are few; the balance of strength is against us.

sentences.zh: 今若畏懦不進，必為所乘，雖至尋陽，豈能自固。

translations.literal: If now we fear and shrink and do not advance, we will surely be overcome by them; even if we reach Xunyang, how can we hold firm?
translations.idiomatic: If we shrink back now, they will surely overcome us; even at Xunyang we could not hold.

sentences.zh: 玄雖竊名雄豪，內實恇怯，加已經奔敗，眾無固心。

translations.literal: Although Xuan usurps the name of a bold hero, inwardly he is truly timid and fearful; moreover he has already fled in defeat, and the masses have no firm heart.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan may pose as a bold hero, but inwardly he is timid; he has already fled in defeat, and his men have no firm heart.

sentences.zh: 決機兩陣，將雄者克。

translations.literal: When the moment is decided between two battle lines, the commander who is bold conquers.
translations.idiomatic: When two armies meet in decisive battle, the bolder commander wins.

sentences.zh: 昔光武昆陽之戰，曹操官渡之師，皆以少制多，共所聞也。

translations.literal: In the past Guangwu at the battle of Kunyang and Cao Cao at the army of Guandu both used the few to overcome the many—this is what all have heard.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu at Kunyang and Cao Cao at Guandu both used the few to overcome the many—everyone knows those stories.

sentences.zh: 今雖才謝古人，豈可先為之弱！」

translations.literal: Though today our talent falls short of the ancients, how can we first show ourselves weak before them!"
translations.idiomatic: Though we fall short of the ancients, how can we show weakness first!"

sentences.zh: 因麾眾而進，毅等從之，大破玄軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he waved the troops forward; Yi and the others followed, and Xuan's army was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He waved the troops forward; Yi and the others followed, and Xuan's army was routed.

sentences.zh: 郭銓與玄單舸走，江陵不復能守，欲入蜀，為馮遷所斬。

translations.literal: Guo Quan fled with Xuan in a single boat; Jiangling could no longer be held; wishing to enter Shu, he was beheaded by Feng Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Quan fled with Xuan in a single boat; Jiangling could no longer be held; heading for Shu, he was beheaded by Feng Qian.

sentences.zh: 義軍遇風不進，桓謙、桓振復據江陵，毅留巴陵，道規與無忌俱進攻桓謐於馬頭，桓蔚於寵洲，皆破之。

translations.literal: The righteous army met wind and could not advance; Huan Qian and Huan Zhen again held Jiangling; Yi remained at Baling; Daogui and Wuji together advanced to attack Huan Mi at Matou and Huan Wei at Chongzhou, and defeated them both.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal army was halted by wind; Huan Qian and Huan Zhen seized Jiangling again; Yi held Baling while Daogui and Wuji attacked Huan Mi at Matou and Huan Wei at Chongzhou and defeated them both.

sentences.zh: 無忌欲乘勝直造江陵，道規曰：「兵法屈申有時，不可苟進。

translations.literal: Wuji wanted to ride the victory straight to Jiangling; Daogui said: "In the art of war bending and extending have their seasons; one cannot advance rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji wanted to press straight on to Jiangling; Daogui said: "In war advance and retreat have their seasons; one cannot rush ahead rashly.

sentences.zh: 諸桓世居西楚，群小皆為竭力，振勇冠三軍，難與爭勝。

translations.literal: The Huan clan for generations dwelt in western Chu; the lesser men all exert themselves to the utmost; Zhen's courage tops the three armies—hard to contend with for victory.
translations.idiomatic: The Huans have long ruled western Chu; their followers fight with all their strength; Zhen's courage tops the three armies—it will be hard to defeat him in open battle.

sentences.zh: 且可頓兵養銳，徐以計策縻之，不憂不克也。」

translations.literal: For the present we can halt the troops and nourish sharpness, and slowly with stratagems tie him down—no worry that we will not overcome."
translations.idiomatic: For now we should halt, rest the troops, and wear him down with strategy—we need not fear that we will not prevail."

sentences.zh: 無忌不從，果為振所敗。

translations.literal: Wuji did not follow this advice and was indeed defeated by Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji would not listen and was indeed defeated by Zhen.

sentences.zh: 乃退還尋陽，繕治舟甲，復進軍夏口。

translations.literal: They then withdrew to Xunyang, repaired ships and armor, and again advanced the army to Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew to Xunyang, repaired ships and armor, and advanced again on Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 偽鎮軍將軍馮該戍夏口東岸，揚武將軍孟山圖據魯城，輔國將軍桓仙客守偃月壘。

translations.literal: The false General Who Guards the Army Feng Gai garrisoned the east bank of Xiakou; General Who Displays Martiality Meng Shantu held Lucheng; General Who Supports the State Huan Xianke guarded Waning Moon Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: The puppet General Who Guards the Army Feng Gai held the east bank of Xiakou; General Who Displays Martiality Meng Shantu held Lucheng; General Who Supports the State Huan Xianke guarded Waning Moon Fortress.

sentences.zh: 於是毅攻魯城，道規、無忌攻偃月，並克之，生禽仙客、山圖。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yi attacked Lucheng; Daogui and Wuji attacked Waning Moon; both were taken, and Xianke and Shantu were captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: Yi attacked Lucheng while Daogui and Wuji attacked Waning Moon; both fell, and Xianke and Shantu were captured alive.

sentences.zh: 其夕，該遁走，進平巴陵。

translations.literal: That evening Gai fled in stealth; they advanced and pacified Baling.
translations.idiomatic: That evening Gai fled; they advanced and pacified Baling.

sentences.zh: 謙、振遣使求割荊、江二州，奉歸晉帝，不許。

translations.literal: Qian and Zhen sent envoys asking to cede the two provinces of Jing and Jiang and return allegiance to the Jin emperor; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Qian and Zhen sent envoys offering to cede Jing and Jiang and return allegiance to the Jin emperor; the offer was refused.

sentences.zh: 會南陽太守魯宗之起義攻襄陽，偽雍州刺史桓蔚走江陵。

translations.literal: At this time Nanyang Administrator Lu Zongzhi rose in righteous revolt to attack Xiangyang; the false Inspector of Yongzhou Huan Wei fled to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Nanyang administrator Lu Zongzhi rose in revolt against Xiangyang; the puppet inspector of Yongzhou Huan Wei fled to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 宗之進至紀南，振自往距之，使桓謙留守。

translations.literal: Zongzhi advanced to Jinan; Zhen went in person to block him and left Huan Qian to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhi advanced to Jinan; Zhen went in person to block him and left Huan Qian to hold Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 時毅、道規已次馬頭，馳往襲，謙奔走，即日克江陵城。

translations.literal: At that time Yi and Daogui had already halted at Matou; they galloped to strike; Qian fled in panic, and that same day Jiangling city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and Daogui had already halted at Matou; they galloped to strike; Qian fled, and Jiangling fell the same day.

sentences.zh: 振大破宗之而歸，聞城已陷，亦走。

translations.literal: Zhen greatly defeated Zongzhi and returned; hearing the city had fallen, he fled as well.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen routed Zongzhi and returned; hearing the city had fallen, he fled as well.

sentences.zh: 無忌翼衛天子還京師，道規留夏口。

translations.literal: Wuji escorted the Son of Heaven back to the capital; Daogui remained at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji escorted the emperor back to the capital; Daogui remained at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 江陵之平也，道規推毅為元功，無忌為次功，自居其末。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified, Daogui ranked Yi as the primary merit-holder and Wuji as secondary merit, placing himself last.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, Daogui credited Liu Yi with the greatest merit and He Wuji with the second rank, putting himself last.

sentences.zh: 進號輔國將軍、督淮北諸軍事、并州刺史，義昌太守如故。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Assists the State, overseer of military affairs in all Huaibei, and Inspector of Bingzhou; Administrator of Yichang remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Assists the State, given oversight of military affairs in Huaibei and made inspector of Bingzhou, while remaining administrator of Yichang.

sentences.zh: 時荊州、湘、江、豫猶多桓氏餘燼，往往屯結。

translations.literal: At that time Jingzhou, Xiang, Jiang, and Yu still had many embers of the Huan clan, often gathering in encampments.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, Xiang, the Jiang region, and Yu still harbored many Huan loyalists who often formed armed bands.

sentences.zh: 復以本官進督江州之武昌、荊州之江夏、隨郡、義陽、綏安、豫州之西陽、汝南、潁川、新蔡九郡諸軍事，隨宜剪撲，皆悉平之。

translations.literal: Again with his existing office he was advanced to oversee military affairs of the nine commanderies—Wuchang in Jiangzhou; Jiangxia, Suixian, Yiyang, and Sui'an in Jingzhou; and Xiyang, Runan, Yingchuan, and Xincai in Yuzhou—cutting down and destroying as suited; all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He was further authorized in his existing post to oversee military affairs in nine commanderies—Wuchang in Jiangzhou; Jiangxia, Suixian, Yiyang, and Sui'an in Jingzhou; and Xiyang, Runan, Yingchuan, and Xincai in Yuzhou—and crushed resistance wherever he found it until all were pacified.

sentences.zh: 以義勳封華容縣公，食邑三千戶。

translations.literal: For righteous merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Huarong county with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was enfeoffed as Duke of Huarong county with three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 遷使持節、都督荊、寧、秦、梁、雍六州、司州之河南諸軍事、領護南蠻校尉、荊州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, overseer of military affairs in the six provinces Jing, Ning, Qin, Liang, and Yong and Henan in Sizhou, concurrently Colonel Who Protects the Southern Man and Inspector of Jingzhou; his generalship was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was made bearer of the staff of authority and overseer of military affairs in Jing, Ning, Qin, Liang, Yong, and Henan in Sizhou, while retaining his post as colonel protecting the southern tribes and inspector of Jingzhou; his general's title was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 辭南蠻以授殷叔文。

translations.literal: He resigned the Southern Man colonelcy and gave it to Yin Shuwen.
translations.idiomatic: He relinquished the southern tribes colonelcy to Yin Shuwen.

sentences.zh: 叔文被誅，乃復還領。

translations.literal: When Shuwen was executed, he then resumed holding it.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuwen was executed, he resumed the post.

sentences.zh: 善於為治，刑政明理，士民莫不畏而愛之。

translations.literal: He was skilled in governance; punishments and administration were clear and orderly, and gentry and commoners all feared and yet loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed well: law and administration were clear, and scholars and commoners alike feared yet loved him.

sentences.zh: 劉敬宣征蜀不克，道規以督統降為建威將軍。

translations.literal: Liu Jingxuan's campaign against Shu did not succeed; Daogui for his supervisory command was reduced to General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jingxuan's Shu campaign failed, Daogui's supervisory authority was reduced and he became General Who Establishes Might.

sentences.zh: 盧循寇逼京邑，道規遣司馬王鎮之及揚武將軍檀道濟、廣武將軍到彥之等赴援朝廷，至尋陽，為賊黨荀林所破。

translations.literal: Lu Xun raided and pressed the capital region; Daogui sent the Major Wang Zhenzhi and the Generals Who Display Martiality Tan Daoji and Who Display Martial Might Dao Yanzhi and others to go rescue the court; they reached Xunyang and were defeated by the rebel partisan Xun Lin.
translations.idiomatic: As Lu Xun threatened the capital, Daogui sent Registrar Wang Zhenzhi with Generals Tan Daoji and Dao Yanzhi and others to reinforce the court; at Xunyang they were defeated by the rebel partisan Xun Lin.

sentences.zh: 循即以林為南蠻校尉，分兵配之。

translations.literal: Xun at once made Lin Colonel of the Southern Man and allotted troops to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun immediately appointed Lin colonel of the southern tribes and assigned him troops.

sentences.zh: 使乘勝伐江陵，揚聲云徐道覆已克京邑。

translations.literal: He had them press the victory to attack Jiangling, proclaiming loudly that Xu Daofu had already taken the capital.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on toward Jiangling, spreading word that Xu Daofu had already seized the capital.

sentences.zh: 而桓謙自長安入蜀，譙縱以謙為荊州刺史，厚加資給，與其大將譙道福俱寇江陵，正與林會。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Huan Qian entered Shu from Chang'an; Qiao Zong made Qian Inspector of Jingzhou, richly supplied him, and together with his great general Qiao Daofu both raided Jiangling, just meeting Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Huan Qian came from Chang'an into Shu; Qiao Zong made him inspector of Jingzhou, richly supplied him, and with his chief general Qiao Daofu marched on Jiangling—just as Lin arrived.

sentences.zh: 林屯江津，謙軍枝江，二寇交逼，分絕都邑之間。

translations.literal: Lin encamped at Jiangjin; Qian's army at Zhijiang; the two foes pressed together, cutting off the space between the capital and towns.
translations.idiomatic: Lin encamped at Jiangjin and Qian at Zhijiang; the two foes pressed in together and severed the routes between the city and outlying settlements.

sentences.zh: 荊楚既桓氏義舊，並懷異心。

translations.literal: Jing and Chu were already old associates of the Huan clan; all harbored other hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing-Chu region was full of former Huan associates, and all nursed divided loyalties.

sentences.zh: 道規乃會將士，告之曰：「桓謙今在近畿，聞者頗有去就之計。

translations.literal: Daogui then gathered officers and men and told them: "Huan Qian is now in the near suburbs; those who hear of it largely have plans to leave or stay.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui assembled his officers and addressed them: "Huan Qian is close at hand, and many are already weighing whether to stay or go.

sentences.zh: 吾東來文武，足以濟事。

translations.literal: Our civil and military who came east are sufficient to accomplish the task.
translations.idiomatic: The civil and military men I brought from the east are enough to see this through.

sentences.zh: 若欲去者，本不相禁。」

translations.literal: If you wish to leave, I will not forbid it in the first place."
translations.idiomatic: If anyone wishes to leave, I will not stop you."

sentences.zh: 因夜開城門，達曉不閉，眾咸憚服，莫有去者。

translations.literal: Thereupon at night he opened the city gates; until dawn he did not close them; all feared and submitted, and none left.
translations.idiomatic: That night he opened the city gates and left them open until dawn; all were awed into loyalty, and none left.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史魯宗之率眾數千自襄陽來赴。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yongzhou Lu Zongzhi led several thousand men from Xiangyang to come to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zongzhi, inspector of Yongzhou, led several thousand men from Xiangyang to join him.

sentences.zh: 或謂宗之未可測，道規乃單馬迎之，宗之感悅。

translations.literal: Some said Zongzhi could not be gauged; Daogui then went out alone on horseback to meet him, and Zongzhi was moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Some warned that Zongzhi's intentions were uncertain; Daogui rode out alone to meet him, and Zongzhi was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 眾議欲使檀道濟、到彥之與宗之共擊，道規曰：「盧循擁隔中流，扇張同異，桓謙、荀林更相首尾。

translations.literal: The assembly discussed having Tan Daoji, Dao Yanzhi, and Zongzhi strike together; Daogui said: "Lu Xun holds the midstream and blocks passage, fanning division and difference; Huan Qian and Xun Lin support each other in head and tail.
translations.idiomatic: The officers proposed sending Tan Daoji, Dao Yanzhi, and Zongzhi to attack together; Daogui said: "Lu Xun holds the midstream and stirs up division; Huan Qian and Xun Lin are backing each other.

sentences.zh: 人懷危懼，莫有固心，成敗之機，在此一舉。

translations.literal: Men harbor fear and dread; none have a firm heart; the moment of success or failure hangs on this one move.
translations.idiomatic: The men are afraid and unsettled; success or failure hangs on this one stroke.

sentences.zh: 非吾自行，其事不決。」

translations.literal: Unless I go myself, the matter will not be decided."
translations.idiomatic: Unless I go in person, this will not be settled."

sentences.zh: 乃使宗之居守，委以腹心，率諸軍攻謙。

translations.literal: He then had Zongzhi remain to guard, entrusted him as his innermost confidant, and led the armies to attack Qian.
translations.idiomatic: He left Zongzhi to hold the city, entrusted him with full authority, and led the army against Qian.

sentences.zh: 諸將佐皆固諫曰：「今遠出討謙，其勝難必。

translations.literal: All generals and aides firmly remonstrated, saying: "Now going far out to attack Qian, victory is hard to assure.
translations.idiomatic: His generals all urged him firmly: "Marching far to attack Qian, victory is far from certain.

sentences.zh: 荀林近在江津，伺人動靜。

translations.literal: Xun Lin is near at Jiangjin, watching men's movements.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Lin is close at Jiangjin, watching our every move.

sentences.zh: 若來攻城，宗之未必能固，脫有差跌，大事去矣。」

translations.literal: If he comes to attack the city, Zongzhi may not be able to hold firm; if by chance there is a slip, the great affair is lost."
translations.idiomatic: If he attacks the city, Zongzhi may not hold; one misstep and all is lost."

sentences.zh: 道規曰：「諸君不識兵機耳。

translations.literal: Daogui said: "Gentlemen, you do not understand the mechanisms of war.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui said: "You do not understand military timing.

sentences.zh: 荀林愚豎，無它奇計。

translations.literal: Xun Lin is a foolish fellow; he has no other clever plan.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Lin is a fool with no clever schemes.

sentences.zh: 以吾去未遠，必不敢向城。

translations.literal: Because I have not gone far, he will certainly not dare turn toward the city.
translations.idiomatic: While I am still near, he will not dare strike the city.

sentences.zh: 吾今取謙，往至便克，沈疑之間，已自還反。

translations.literal: If I now take Qian, going there I will conquer at once; in the interval of hesitation and doubt, I will already have returned.
translations.idiomatic: I will take Qian now—reach him and win at once—and be back before he can even hesitate.

sentences.zh: 謙敗則林破膽，豈暇得來？。

translations.literal: When Qian is defeated, Lin's courage will be broken—how would he have leisure to come?
translations.idiomatic: Once Qian falls, Lin will lose his nerve—how could he find time to attack?
