sentences.zh: 且宗之獨守，何為不支數日。」

translations.literal: Moreover, with Zongzhi holding alone, why could he not sustain it for several days?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Zongzhi alone can surely hold for several days."

sentences.zh: 解南蠻校尉印以授諮議參軍劉遵。

translations.literal: He removed the seal of Colonel of the Southern Man and gave it to the Advising Staff Officer Liu Zun.
translations.idiomatic: He handed the southern tribes colonel's seal to his advising staff officer Liu Zun.

sentences.zh: 馳往攻謙，水陸齊進。

translations.literal: He galloped to attack Qian, advancing together by water and land.
translations.idiomatic: He raced to attack Qian by land and water together.

sentences.zh: 謙大敗，單舸走，欲下就林，追斬之。

translations.literal: Qian was greatly defeated, fled in a single boat, wished to go down to join Lin, and was pursued and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was routed, fled alone by boat toward Lin's position, and was pursued and killed.

sentences.zh: 還至浦口，林又奔散。

translations.literal: Returning to Pukou, Lin again fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: On the return to Pukou, Lin had already broken and fled.

sentences.zh: 劉遵率軍追林，至巴陵，斬之。

translations.literal: Liu Zun led the army in pursuit of Lin; reaching Baling, he beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zun pursued Lin to Baling and killed him.

sentences.zh: 初，謙至枝江，江陵士庶皆與謙書，言城內虛實，咸欲謀為內應。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qian reached Zhijiang, gentry and commoners of Jiangling all wrote letters to Qian telling the truth and falsehood within the city; all wished to plot as inner responders.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Qian reached Zhijiang, Jiangling's elite and commoners wrote to him with inside intelligence, all plotting to open the gates from within.

sentences.zh: 至是參軍曹仲宗檢得之，道規悉焚不視，眾於是大安。

translations.literal: At this time the staff officer Cao Zhongzong examined and obtained them; Daogui burned them all without reading; the masses thereupon were greatly reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Cao Zhongzong then discovered the letters; Daogui burned them unread, and the people were greatly reassured.

sentences.zh: 進號征西將軍。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Conquers the West.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Conquers the West.

sentences.zh: 先是，桓歆子道兒逃於江西，出擊義陽郡，與盧循相連接，循使蔡猛助之。

translations.literal: Before this, Huan Xin's son Dao'er had fled to the west of the river, came out to attack Yiyang commandery, connected with Lu Xun, and Xun sent Cai Meng to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Huan Xin's son Dao'er had fled to Jiangxi, raided Yiyang commandery, linked up with Lu Xun, and Xun sent Cai Meng to support him.

sentences.zh: 道規遣參軍劉基破道兒於大薄，臨陳斬猛。

translations.literal: Daogui sent the staff officer Liu Ji to defeat Dao'er at Dabo and beheaded Meng on the battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui sent staff officer Liu Ji to defeat Dao'er at Dabo and killed Meng in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 徐道覆率眾三萬，奄至破冢，魯宗之已還襄陽，追召不及，人情大震。

translations.literal: Xu Daofu led thirty thousand men and suddenly arrived at Pojia; Lu Zongzhi had already returned to Xiangyang and could not be recalled in pursuit; popular sentiment was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daofu led thirty thousand men in a sudden strike at Pojia; Lu Zongzhi had already returned to Xiangyang and could not be recalled in time, and morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 或傳循已平京師，遣道覆上為刺史，江漢士庶感焚書之恩，無復貳志。

translations.literal: Some spread word that Xun had already pacified the capital and sent Daofu up as inspector; gentry and commoners of Jiang and Han felt the grace of the burned letters and had no second thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread that Xun had taken the capital and sent Daofu north as inspector; but the people of the Jiang and Han remembered Daogui's grace in burning the treasonous letters, and none wavered.

sentences.zh: 道規使劉遵為游軍，自距道覆於豫章口。

translations.literal: Daogui made Liu Zun a mobile corps and himself barred Daofu at the mouth of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui deployed Liu Zun as a mobile force and himself blocked Daofu at the mouth of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 前驅失利，道規壯氣愈厲，激揚三軍；

translations.literal: The vanguard was defeated; Daogui's bold spirit grew fiercer still, rousing the three armies.
translations.idiomatic: When the vanguard faltered, Daogui's resolve only hardened, and he roused the whole army.

sentences.zh: 遵自外橫擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Zun from outside struck across and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Zun struck from the flank and routed them.

sentences.zh: 斬首萬餘級，赴水死者殆盡，道覆單舸走還盆口。

translations.literal: Heads cut numbered more than ten thousand; those who entered the water to die were nearly all; Daofu fled in a single boat back to Penkou.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand were killed, and nearly all who fled into the river drowned; Daofu escaped alone by boat back to Penkou.

sentences.zh: 初使遵為游軍，眾咸云：「今強敵在前，唯患眾少，不應割削見力，置無用之地。」

translations.literal: When he first made Zun a mobile corps, all said: "Now with a strong foe before us, the only worry is too few men; one should not cut away present strength and place it in a useless position."
translations.idiomatic: When he first assigned Zun as a mobile force, many objected: "With a strong enemy before us, we already lack numbers—why strip strength away and park it where it cannot help?"

sentences.zh: 及破道覆，果得游軍之力，眾乃服焉。

translations.literal: When Daofu was defeated, they indeed gained the mobile corps' strength; the masses then submitted in conviction.
translations.idiomatic: After Daofu was beaten, the mobile force proved decisive, and all were convinced.

sentences.zh: 遵字慧明，臨淮海西人，道規從母兄蕭氏舅也。

translations.literal: Zun, courtesy name Huiming, was a man of Haixi in Linhuai; he was Daogui's maternal cousin on the Xiao side.
translations.idiomatic: Zun, styled Huiming, was from Haixi in Linhuai and was Daogui's maternal cousin of the Xiao clan.

sentences.zh: 官至右將軍、宣城內史、淮南太守。

translations.literal: He reached the offices of General of the Right, Interior Minister of Xuancheng, and Administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General of the Right, interior minister of Xuancheng, and administrator of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 義熙十年，卒，追贈撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yixi he died; posthumously he was given General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yixi 10 and was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 追封監利縣侯，食邑七百戶。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jianli county with a fief of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Jianli county with seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 道規進號征西大將軍、開府儀同三司，加散騎常侍，固辭。

translations.literal: Daogui's title was advanced to Grand General Who Conquers the West and Master of Affairs with Credentials Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers; he was given Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui was promoted to Grand General Who Conquers the West with credentials equal to the Three Ducal Ministers and made cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, but he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 俄而寢疾，改授都督豫、江二州、揚州之宣城、淮南、盧江、歷陽、安豐、堂邑六郡諸軍事、豫州刺史，持節、常侍、將軍如故。

translations.literal: Shortly he took to bed with illness; he was reassigned as overseer of military affairs in the two provinces Yu and Jiang and the six commanderies Xuancheng, Huainan, Lujiang, Liyang, Anfeng, and Tangyi in Yangzhou, and Inspector of Yuzhou; bearer of the staff, cavalier attendant, and general remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he fell ill and was reassigned to oversee military affairs in Yu and Jiang and six Yangzhou commanderies—Xuancheng, Huainan, Lujiang, Liyang, Anfeng, and Tangyi—and made inspector of Yuzhou, while retaining his staff, cavalier attendant, and general's titles.

sentences.zh: 以疾不拜。

translations.literal: Because of illness he did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Illness kept him from taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 八年閏月，薨於京師，時年四十三，

translations.literal: In the intercalary month of the eighth year he died at the capital, aged forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month of Yixi 8 he died at the capital, aged forty-three.

sentences.zh: 追贈侍中、司徒，加班劍二十人。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, with twenty ceremonial sword attendants added.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was given Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, with twenty ceremonial sword attendants added.

sentences.zh: 諡曰烈武公。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Duke Lie Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Duke Lie Wu.

sentences.zh: 平桓謙功，進封南郡公，邑五千戶。

translations.literal: For the merit of pacifying Huan Qian he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Nan commandery with a fief of five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For defeating Huan Qian he was advanced to Duke of Nan commandery with five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，贈大司馬，追封臨川王，食邑如先。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu received the Mandate, he was given Grand Marshal and posthumously enfeoffed as King of Linchuan, with a fief as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, Daogui was posthumously made Grand Marshal and King of Linchuan, with the same fief as before.

sentences.zh: 道規無子，以長沙景王第二子義慶為嗣。

translations.literal: Daogui had no son; he took the second son of Prince Jing of Changsha, Yiqing, as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui had no sons; Yiqing, second son of Prince Jing of Changsha, was made his heir.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖少為道規所養，高祖命紹焉，咸以禮無二繼，太祖還本，而定義慶為後。

translations.literal: Earlier the Taizu in youth was raised by Daogui; the Gaozu ordered him to succeed, but all said rites allow no double succession; the Taizu returned to his original line, and Yiqing was fixed as heir.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu had been raised by Daogui in youth, and the Gaozu first ordered him to succeed; but ritual forbids two lines of succession, so the Taizu returned to his birth family and Yiqing was confirmed as heir.

sentences.zh: 義慶為荊州，廟主當隨往江陵，太祖詔曰：「褒崇道勳，經國之盛典；

translations.literal: When Yiqing was in Jingzhou, the temple lord was to follow to Jiangling; the Taizu issued an edict: "Honoring and exalting the Way's merit is a canonical ceremony of governing the state;
translations.idiomatic: When Yiqing went to Jingzhou, the ancestral tablet was to move with him to Jiangling; the Taizu issued an edict: "Honoring meritorious service is a canonical state ceremony;

sentences.zh: 尊親追遠，因心之所隆。

translations.literal: honoring kin and pursuing the distant is what the heart exalts.
translations.idiomatic: and revering kin and honoring the dead is what the heart most esteems.

sentences.zh: 故侍中、大司馬臨川烈武王，體道欽明，至德淵邈，叡哲自天，孝友光備。

translations.literal: The late Palace Attendant, Grand Marshal, King Lie Wu of Linchuan embodied the Way, was reverent and bright, of utmost virtue deep and far, sagely wise from Heaven, filial and brotherly in full radiance.
translations.idiomatic: The late Palace Attendant and Grand Marshal, King Lie Wu of Linchuan, embodied the Way, was reverent and wise, of profound virtue, sagely gifted by Heaven, and complete in filial piety and brotherly duty.

sentences.zh: 爰始協規，則翼贊景業；

translations.literal: From the first he joined in planning, then aided and praised the founding enterprise;
translations.idiomatic: From the first he helped plan and supported the founding enterprise;

sentences.zh: 陵威致討，則克剪梟鯨。

translations.literal: when majesty was overborne and punishment was launched, he cut down and clipped the owls and whales.
translations.idiomatic: when rebels had to be crushed, he cut down the fiercest foes.

sentences.zh: 逮妖逆交侵，方難孔棘，勢逾累綦，人無固志。

translations.literal: When demon rebels pressed together, the realm's hardship was greatly thorny, the situation more urgent than piled weights, and men had no firm will.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels pressed in from every side, the realm was in grave peril, the crisis piled ever higher, and men's hearts wavered.

sentences.zh: 王神謨獨運，靈武宏發，輯寧內外，誅覆群凶，固已化被江漢，勳高微管，遠猷侔於二南，英雄邁於兩獻者矣。

translations.literal: The king alone deployed divine stratagems; numinous martiality burst forth greatly; he gathered peace within and without, executed and overthrew the flock of villains—already his transforming influence covered Jiang and Han, his merit higher than Wei and Guan, his far-reaching plans equal to the Two Souths, his heroism surpassing the Two Xians.
translations.idiomatic: He alone wielded divine strategy and mighty arms, restored peace within and without, and destroyed the rebel hosts—his influence spread across the Jiang and Han, his merit outshone Guan Zhong, his vision matched the Zhou poets, and his heroism surpassed the ancient worthies.

sentences.zh: 朕幼蒙殊愛，德廕特隆，豐恩慈訓，義深情戚，永惟仁範，感慕纏懷。

translations.literal: I in youth received special love; virtue's shade was especially lofty; abundant grace and kindly instruction, righteousness deep and feeling kin—forever recalling his humane model, moved and longing twine in the breast.
translations.idiomatic: I was cherished in youth and deeply indebted to his kindness and teaching; his righteousness and affection bind my heart, and I forever recall his humane example with enduring grief.

sentences.zh: 今當擁移寢祏，初祀西夏，思崇嘉禮，式備徽章，庶以昭宣風度，允副幽顯。

translations.literal: Now we are to embrace and move the sleeping spirit tablet, first sacrifice in the western summer—thinking to exalt fine rites, fully prepare emblems and insignia, hoping thereby to proclaim and display his bearing, truly answering both hidden and manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Now, as his spirit tablet is to be moved and first sacrifices offered in the west, I wish to honor him with full ceremony and proper insignia, that his stature may be proclaimed to the living and the dead alike.

sentences.zh: 其追崇丞相，加殊禮，鸞輅九旒，黃屋左纛，給節鉞、前後部羽葆、鼓吹、虎賁班劍百人，侍中如故。」

translations.literal: Let him be posthumously exalted as Chancellor, with extraordinary rites: imperial carriage with nine tassels, yellow canopy and left banner, given staff and axe, front and rear feather parasols, drums and pipes, one hundred tiger-guard ceremonial sword attendants; Palace Attendant as before."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously honored as Chancellor with extraordinary rites: the imperial carriage with nine tassels, yellow canopy and left banner, staff and battle-axe, front and rear feather parasols, drums and pipes, one hundred tiger-guard ceremonial sword attendants, and his palace attendant title retained."

sentences.zh: 及長沙太妃檀氏、臨川太妃曹氏後薨，祭皆給鸞輅九旒，黃屋左纛，轀輬車，挽歌一部，前後部羽葆、鼓吹，虎賁班劍百人。

translations.literal: When the Grand Consort of Changsha, Lady Tan, and the Grand Consort of Linchuan, Lady Cao, later died, their sacrifices all were given imperial carriage with nine tassels, yellow canopy and left banner, covered transport cart, one set of funeral dirges, front and rear feather parasols and drums and pipes, and one hundred tiger-guard ceremonial sword attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When the grand consorts of Changsha, Lady Tan, and of Linchuan, Lady Cao, died later, their funeral rites likewise included the nine-tasseled imperial carriage, yellow canopy and left banner, covered funeral cart, a full dirge choir, front and rear feather parasols and drums and pipes, and one hundred tiger-guard ceremonial sword attendants.

sentences.zh: 義慶幼為高祖所知，常曰：「此吾家豐城也。」

translations.literal: Yiqing in youth was known to the Gaozu, who often said: "This is our family's Fengcheng."
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozu noticed Yiqing early and often said: "This is our family's Fengcheng sword."

sentences.zh: 年十三，襲封南郡公。

translations.literal: At age thirteen he succeeded to the enfeoffment as Duke of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he succeeded to the dukedom of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 除給事，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant, but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed attendant but declined the post.

sentences.zh: 義熙十二年，從伐長安，還拜輔國將軍、北青州刺史，未之任，徙督豫州諸軍事、豫州刺史，復督淮北諸軍事，豫州刺史、將軍竝如故。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yixi he followed the campaign against Chang'an; on return he was appointed General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Northern Qingzhou; he did not go to the post; he was transferred to oversee military affairs in Yuzhou and made Inspector of Yuzhou; again he oversaw military affairs in Huaibei; Inspector of Yuzhou and general both remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 12 he joined the campaign against Chang'an; on his return he was made General Who Assists the State and inspector of northern Qingzhou but never took up the post, then was transferred to oversee Yuzhou and made its inspector, with continued oversight of Huaibei; his general's title was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 永初元年，襲封臨川王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchu he succeeded to enfeoffment as King of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu 1 he succeeded as King of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 徵為侍中。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 元嘉元年，轉散騎常侍，秘書監，徙度支尚書，遷丹陽尹，加輔國將軍、常侍竝如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanjia he was transferred to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Secretariat; he moved to Minister of Revenue, was promoted to Governor of Danyang, and given General Who Assists the State; cavalier attendant both remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanjia he became cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and director of the Secretariat, then minister of revenue, then governor of Danyang, while retaining his post as General Who Assists the State and cavalier attendant.

sentences.zh: 時有民黃初妻趙殺子婦，遇赦應徙送避孫讎。

translations.literal: At that time a commoner, Zhao, wife of Huang Chu, killed her daughter-in-law; encountering an amnesty she should have been banished and sent away to avoid the grandson's vengeance.
translations.idiomatic: A woman named Zhao, wife of a commoner Huang Chu, had killed her daughter-in-law; under an amnesty she was to be exiled so the grandson could avoid facing his grandmother.

sentences.zh: 義慶曰：「案《周禮》，父母之讎，避之海外，雖遇市朝，鬬不及兵。

translations.literal: Yiqing said: "According to the Rites of Zhou, a parent's enemy is to be avoided overseas; even if one meets in market or court, one does not fight with weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing said: "The Rites of Zhou hold that one must avoid a parent's enemy even overseas, and even in market or court one does not take up arms against them.

sentences.zh: 蓋以莫大之冤，理不可奪，含戚枕戈，義許必報。

translations.literal: This is because for a grievance without measure, reason cannot be taken away; bearing grief and sleeping on a spear, righteousness permits that revenge must be taken.
translations.idiomatic: For so great a wrong, justice cannot be denied: sleeping on a spear in grief, one is bound to take revenge.

sentences.zh: 至於親戚為戮，骨肉相殘，故道乖常憲，記無定準，求之法外，裁以人情。

translations.literal: As for kin slaughtering kin and flesh-and-bone harming one another, therefore the Way departs from constant statutes, records have no fixed standard, and one seeks outside the law, judging by human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: When kin kill kin, the usual law no longer applies; records offer no fixed rule, and one must judge beyond the code by human feeling.

sentences.zh: 且禮有過失之宥，律無讎祖之文。

translations.literal: Moreover rites have pardon for offenses, but statutes have no text on avenging a grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: Rites allow pardon for offenses, but the statutes say nothing about avenging a grandmother.

sentences.zh: 況趙之縱暴，本由於酒，論心即實，事盡荒耄。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhao's indulging in violence arose from wine; judging the heart as fact, the affair was entirely the confusion of extreme age.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Zhao's violence arose from drink; in intent and fact the whole affair was the folly of extreme old age.

sentences.zh: 豈得以荒耄之王母，等行路之深讎。

translations.literal: How can one take a grandmother confused in extreme age and equate her with a passerby's deep enemy?
translations.idiomatic: How can a senile grandmother be treated like a stranger's mortal enemy?

sentences.zh: 臣謂此孫忍愧銜悲，不違子義，共天同域，無虧孝道。」

translations.literal: Your servant holds that this grandson, bearing shame and holding grief, does not violate the son's righteousness; sharing Heaven and the same realm, he does not fall short of filial piety."
translations.idiomatic: I hold that this grandson, bearing shame and grief, does not violate a son's duty; living under the same Heaven in the same realm, he does not fall short of filial piety."

sentences.zh: 六年，加尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was given Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanjia he was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 八年，太白星犯右執法，義慶懼有災禍，乞求外鎮。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Great White star violated the Right Enforcer; Yiqing feared disaster and begged for an outer garrison post.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanjia the planet Venus crossed the Right Enforcer; fearing calamity, Yiqing asked for a provincial post.

sentences.zh: 太祖詔譬之曰：「玄象茫昧，既難可了。

translations.literal: The Taizu issued an edict to instruct him: "Dark signs are vague and dim; they are already hard to grasp.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu replied by edict: "Heavenly signs are obscure and hard to read.

sentences.zh: 且史家諸占，各有異同，兵星王時，有所干犯，乃主當誅。

translations.literal: Moreover the various prognostications of historians each differ; when the military star reigns in its time, if there is violation, it means the ruler ought to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Historians' prognostications differ, and when the military star is ascendant, such a crossing often means the ruler himself should be punished.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，益無懼也。

translations.literal: Spoken in this way, there is all the more no fear.
translations.idiomatic: By that reading, you have even less cause for fear.

sentences.zh: 鄭僕射亡後，左執法嘗有變，王光祿至今平安。

translations.literal: After Vice Director Zheng died, the Left Enforcer once had a change; Master of Luminosity Wang remains safe to this day.
translations.idiomatic: After Vice Director Zheng died, the Left Enforcer did shift—but Master of Luminosity Wang remains safe to this day.

sentences.zh: 日蝕三朝，天下之至忌，晉孝武初有此異，彼庸主耳，猶竟無他。

translations.literal: An eclipse lasting three days is the utmost taboo under Heaven; Jin Emperor Xiaowu first had this anomaly—he was a mediocre ruler, yet in the end nothing else befell him.
translations.idiomatic: A three-day eclipse is the gravest omen under Heaven; Emperor Xiaowu of Jin was the first to see it—and he was a mediocre ruler, yet nothing worse came of it.

sentences.zh: 天道輔仁福善，謂不足橫生憂懼。

translations.literal: Heaven's Way assists the benevolent and blesses the good—I hold that this is not enough to spawn groundless worry and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven aids the humane and rewards the good; that is no reason to invent fears out of nothing.

sentences.zh: 兄與後軍，各受內外之任，本以維城，表裏經之，盛衰此懷，實有由來之事。

translations.literal: Elder Brother and the Rear Army each bear inner and outer charges, originally to be bulwarks, governing within and without; prosperity and decline rest in this care—truly there is cause in this from of old.
translations.idiomatic: You, my elder brother, and the Rear Army each hold court and field posts, appointed bulwarks of the realm to govern within and without; the dynasty's rise and fall depend on such care—and that has been so from the beginning.

sentences.zh: 設若天必降災，寧可千里逃避邪？

translations.literal: If Heaven must send down disaster, can one flee a thousand li?
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven truly means to send calamity, can you outrun it by fleeing a thousand li?

sentences.zh: 既非遠者之事，又不知吉凶定所；

translations.literal: It is not a matter for fleeing in the first place, nor do we know where fortune or ill is fixed;
translations.idiomatic: Flight is not the answer in any case, nor can anyone know where safety or danger will fall;

sentences.zh: 若在都則有不測，去此必保利貞者，豈敢苟違天邪？」

translations.literal: If in the capital there is the unpredictable, yet leaving here surely preserves fortune and integrity—how dare one casually defy Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: If the capital brings uncertainty but leaving here surely keeps you safe and whole—who would lightly defy Heaven's intent?"

sentences.zh: 義慶固求解僕射，乃許之，加中書令，進號前將軍，常侍、尹如故。

translations.literal: Yiqing firmly asked to be relieved of Vice Director; it was granted. He was additionally made Director of the Secretariat, advanced in title to General of the Van; his posts as Regular Attendant and Metropolitan Governor remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing pressed his request to resign as Vice Director, and permission was granted. He was made Director of the Secretariat and promoted to General of the Van; his posts as Regular Attendant and Metropolitan Governor were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 在京尹九年，出為使持節、都督荊、雍、益、寧、梁、南北秦七州諸軍事、平西將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: After nine years as Metropolitan Governor, he went out as Bearer of the Staff with full powers, Commander over military affairs in the seven provinces of Jing, Yong, Yi, Ning, Liang, and North and South Qin, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years governing the capital, he was sent out with full credential staff as commander of military affairs in Jing, Yong, Yi, Ning, Liang, and North and South Qin, as General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jing.

sentences.zh: 荊州居上流之重，地廣兵強，資實兵甲，居朝廷之半，故高祖使諸子居之。

translations.literal: Jingzhou held the weight of the upper Yangzi: its territory was broad and its troops strong, its stores and armor amounting to half the court's—therefore the Gaozu stationed his sons there.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou commanded the upper Yangzi, a vast territory with powerful armies and stores of grain and arms equal to half the empire—so the Founder posted his sons there.

sentences.zh: 義慶以宗室令美，故特有此授。

translations.literal: Yiqing, for his excellent standing among the imperial clan, received this appointment especially.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing alone received this post because of his outstanding reputation among the princes.

sentences.zh: 性謙虛，始至及去鎮，迎送物竝不受。

translations.literal: By nature he was modest; on first arriving and on leaving his garrison, he accepted none of the gifts for welcoming or seeing off.
translations.idiomatic: He was modest by nature and refused all farewell and welcome gifts both on arriving at and leaving his post.

sentences.zh: 十二年，普使內外群官舉士，義慶上表曰：「詔書疇咨群司，延及連牧，旌賢仄陋，拔善幽遐。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year a general order had inner and outer officials recommend scholars; Yiqing memorialized, saying: "The edict enquires of the multitude of offices, extends to successive governors, honors worthies in humble places, and raises the good from remote depths.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the court ordered officials throughout the empire to recommend scholars; Yiqing memorialized: "Your edict consults every office, reaches successive governors, honors talent in lowly places, and lifts the worthy from far obscurity.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下惠哲光宣，經緯明遠，皇階藻曜，風猷日升，而猶詢衢室之令典，遵明臺之叡訓，降淵慮于管庫，紆聖思乎版築，故以道邈往載，德高前王。

translations.literal: Bowingly: Your Majesty's benevolence and wisdom shine abroad, your weaving of the cosmos is clear and far-reaching, the imperial steps gleam with ornament, your wind and virtue rise day by day—yet you still consult the fine statutes of the Crossroads Chamber, follow the sage teachings of the Bright Tower, lower profound thought to storeroom keepers, and extend holy care to wall-builders; thus your Way surpasses past ages and your virtue towers above former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Your benevolence and wisdom shine across the realm; your governance is far-sighted, the throne radiant, your renown rising daily—yet you still seek counsel as in the Crossroads Chamber, heed the Bright Tower's teaching, bend profound thought to men in storerooms, and extend your mind to men at the mortar; your Way outstrips antiquity and your virtue stands above the kings of old.

sentences.zh: 臣敢竭虛闇，祗承明旨。

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to exhaust my emptiness and dimness, reverently to bear your clear intent.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant dares offer what little he has, reverently to carry out your clear command.

sentences.zh: 伏見前臨沮令新野庾實，秉真履約，愛敬淳深。

translations.literal: Bowing, I have seen the former Magistrate of Linju, Yu Shi of Xinye—he holds truth and walks in restraint, his love and reverence pure and deep.
translations.idiomatic: I have observed Yu Shi of Xinye, former magistrate of Linju: he holds to truth and restraint, his love and reverence deep and sincere.

sentences.zh: 昔在母憂，毀瘠過禮；

translations.literal: Formerly in mourning for his mother, his emaciation exceeded the rites;
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, his grief-wasting exceeded what the rites require;

sentences.zh: 今罹父疚，泣血有聞。

translations.literal: Now afflicted with his father's grief, his weeping blood is heard of.
translations.idiomatic: now in mourning for his father, his weeping until blood flows is known to all.

sentences.zh: 行成閨庭，孝著鄰黨，足以敦化率民，齊教軌俗。

translations.literal: His conduct is formed within the inner quarters, his filial piety renowned in the neighborhood—sufficient to thicken transformation and lead the people, to align teaching and level custom.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct is formed at home, his filial piety known to the neighborhood—enough to deepen custom, guide the people, and set the standard for all.

sentences.zh: 前征奉朝請武陵龔祈，恬和平簡，貞潔純素，潛居研志，耽情墳籍，亦足鎮息頹競，獎勗浮動。

translations.literal: Formerly summoned as Court Gentleman for Imperial Audience, Gong Qi of Wuling—calm, peaceful, and plain, chaste and pure, dwelling in seclusion to grind his will, addicted to the classics in his passion—also sufficient to still declining rivalry and urge on the floating and restless.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Qi of Wuling, formerly summoned as Court Gentleman for Imperial Audience, is calm and plain, chaste and unadorned, living in seclusion to pursue his studies and devoted to the classics—enough as well to steady a declining age and encourage the restless.

sentences.zh: 處士南郡師覺，才學明敏，操介清脩，業均井渫，志固冰霜。

translations.literal: The reclusive scholar Shi Jue of Nan Commandery—his talent and learning bright and keen, his integrity pure and cultivated, his achievement equal to a cleansed well, his resolve firm as frost and ice.
translations.idiomatic: The recluse Shi Jue of Nan Commandery: bright in talent and learning, pure in integrity, his work clean as a swept well, his resolve hard as frost.

sentences.zh: 臣往年辟為州祭酒，未汙其慮。

translations.literal: Your servant in former years summoned him as Libationer of the Province, not yet defiling his intent.
translations.idiomatic: I summoned him last year as provincial Libationer without yet troubling his resolve.

sentences.zh: 若朝命遠暨，玉帛遐臻，異人間出，何遠之有。」

translations.literal: If the court's command reaches far, jade and silk arrive from afar, and extraordinary men appear among the people—what distance is there?"
translations.idiomatic: When the court's call reaches far, gifts and envoys arrive from afar and extraordinary men appear—what place is too remote?"

sentences.zh: 義慶留心撫物，州統內官長親老，不隨在官舍者，年聽遣五吏餉家。

translations.literal: Yiqing gave his heart to comforting the people: within the province, officials whose parents were aged and did not live with them in the official residence were each year allowed to send five clerks to supply their homes.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing cared attentively for his people: officials in the province whose elderly parents did not live with them in their posts were allowed each year to send five clerks home with provisions.

sentences.zh: 先是，王弘為江州，亦有此制。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Hong was in Jiangzhou, there was also this regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong had instituted the same rule when he governed Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 在州八年，為西土所安。

translations.literal: He was in the province eight years and was a source of peace for the western lands.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years in the province won him the trust of the west.

sentences.zh: 撰《徐州先賢傳》十卷，奏上之。

translations.literal: He compiled Records of Former Worthies of Xuzhou in ten scrolls and memorialized it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Records of Former Worthies of Xuzhou in ten scrolls and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 又擬班固《典引》為《典敘》，以述皇代之美。

translations.literal: He also modeled himself on Ban Gu's Canon Introduction to write a Canon Narrative, to narrate the beauty of the imperial age.
translations.idiomatic: He also modeled Ban Gu's Canon Introduction in his Canon Narrative, to celebrate the glories of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 十六年，改授散騎常侍、都督江州、豫州之西陽、晉熙、新蔡三郡諸軍事、衛將軍、江州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was reassigned as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander over military affairs in Jiangzhou and the three commanderies of Xiyang, Jinxi, and Xincai in Yuzhou, General of the Guard, and Inspector of Jiangzhou; his credential staff remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was reassigned as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, commander of Jiangzhou and of Xiyang, Jinxi, and Xincai in Yuzhou, as General of the Guard and Inspector of Jiangzhou, with his staff unchanged.

sentences.zh: 十七年，即本號都督南兗、徐、兗、青、冀、幽六州諸軍事、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, under his existing title, he was made Commander over military affairs in the six provinces of Southern Yan, Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, and You, and Inspector of Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was made, under his existing title, commander of the six provinces of Southern Yan, Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, and You, and Inspector of Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 尋加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally given the Befitting Ceremony of the Three Excellencies with an Opening Office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was granted an office with the ceremonial privileges of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 為性簡素，寡嗜欲，愛好文義，文詞雖不多，然足為宗室之表。

translations.literal: In nature he was plain and simple, with few desires; he loved literary meaning. Though his writings were not many, they sufficed to make him the model of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and sparing in desire, he loved letters; though he wrote little, he was enough to stand as the clan's exemplar.

sentences.zh: 受任歷藩，無浮淫之過，唯晚節奉養沙門，頗致費損。

translations.literal: In posts across successive provinces he had no dissolute excess; only in his later years, supporting Buddhist monks, he caused considerable expense.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive provincial posts he showed no dissolute excess; only in his later years did his patronage of monks cost him dearly.

sentences.zh: 少善騎乘，及長，以世路艱難，不復跨馬。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled at riding; when grown, because the world's paths were hard, he no longer mounted a horse.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he rode well; grown older, he found the times too treacherous and never mounted a horse again.

sentences.zh: 招聚文學之士，近遠必至。

translations.literal: He gathered literary scholars; from near and far they surely came.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered men of letters, and talent came from near and far.

sentences.zh: 太尉袁淑，文冠當時；

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Yuan Shu—his writing crowned the age;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Yuan Shu, whose writing crowned the age;

sentences.zh: 義慶在江州，請為衛軍諮議參軍。

translations.literal: when Yiqing was in Jiangzhou, he requested him as Staff Adviser to the Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: when Yiqing was in Jiangzhou, invited him as Staff Adviser to the Guard General.

sentences.zh: 其餘吳郡陸展、東海何長瑜、鮑照等，並為辭章之美，引為佐史國臣。

translations.literal: The rest—Lu Zhan of Wu Commandery, He Changyu of Donghai, Bao Zhao, and others—were all fine in literary composition; he drew them in as assistant clerks and household retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhan of Wu, He Changyu of Donghai, Bao Zhao, and others were all masters of style; he took them on as secretaries and household retainers.

sentences.zh: 太祖與義慶書，常加意斟酌。

translations.literal: The Taizu, in letters to Yiqing, often paid special care to weigh and revise.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu often weighed and revised his letters to Yiqing with particular care.

sentences.zh: 鮑照，字明遠，文辭贍逸，嘗為古樂府，文甚遒麗。

translations.literal: Bao Zhao, courtesy name Mingyuan—his literary phrasing was rich and unfettered; he once wrote old Music Bureau poems, the writing very forceful and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Zhao, styled Mingyuan, wrote with rich, unfettered eloquence; his old Music Bureau poems are especially forceful and fine.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，河、濟俱清，當時以為美瑞，照為《河清頌》，其序甚工。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era the Yellow River and the Ji both ran clear; the age took this as a beautiful omen. Zhao wrote an Ode on the River Clearing; its preface was very skillful.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanjia era the Yellow River and the Ji ran clear together—a sign of grace. Bao Zhao wrote an Ode on the River Clearing; its preface is a masterwork.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its text says:
translations.idiomatic: The ode reads:

sentences.zh: 臣聞善談天者，必徵象於人；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that one who speaks well of Heaven must verify signs in men;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that those who discourse on Heaven must read its signs in human affairs;

sentences.zh: 工言古者，先考績於今。

translations.literal: one skilled in speaking of antiquity first examines achievement in the present.
translations.idiomatic: and those skilled in antiquity must judge the past by the present.

sentences.zh: 鴻、犧以降，遐哉邈乎，鏤山嶽，雕篆素，昭德垂勳，可謂多矣。

translations.literal: From Hong and Xi down—how far and remote! Mountains carved, plain silk engraved with seal script, virtue proclaimed and merit handed down—one may say there has been much.
translations.idiomatic: From the age of Hong and Xi onward—how remote!—men carved mountains and inscribed silk to proclaim virtue and hand down merit; the record is long indeed.

sentences.zh: 而史編唐堯之功，載「格于上下，」樂登文王之操，稱「於昭于天」。

translations.literal: Yet the histories compile the achievements of Tang Yao, recording "He penetrated above and below;" music ascends to King Wen's airs, praising "How bright in Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the histories praise Tang Yao with "He reached above and below," and music celebrates King Wen with "How glorious before Heaven."

sentences.zh: 素狐玄玉，聿彰符命，朴牛大螾，爰定祥曆，魚鳥動色，禾雉興讓，皆物不盈眥，而美溢金石。

translations.literal: White foxes and dark jade forthwith display the mandate's signs; plain oxen and great earthworms thereby fix the auspicious calendar; fish and birds change color, grain and pheasants rise in yielding—all things not filling the eye's corner, yet beauty overflowing bronze and stone.
translations.idiomatic: White foxes and dark jade proclaimed the mandate; plain oxen and great earthworms fixed the sacred calendar; fish and birds changed hue, grain and pheasants yielded of themselves—omens too slight to fill the eye, yet praise enough to overflow bronze and stone.

sentences.zh: 詩人於是不作，頌聲為之而寢，庸非惑歟。

translations.literal: The poets therefore did not compose; eulogies for this reason fell silent—is this not confusion?
translations.idiomatic: The poets ceased to write; the songs of praise fell still—can this be anything but delusion?

sentences.zh: 自我皇宋之承天命也，仰符應龍之精，俯協河龜之靈，君圖帝寶，粲爛瑰英，固業光曩代，事華前德矣。

translations.literal: From when our August Song received Heaven's mandate, looking up to match the essence of the responsive dragon, looking down to accord with the spirit of the river turtle, the ruler's chart and the imperial treasure blaze in splendor and rare glory—its enterprise surely shines on past ages, its deeds flower above former virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Since our Song received Heaven's mandate, matching above the responsive dragon's essence and below the river turtle's spirit, the imperial design and sacred treasures blaze in splendor—its achievement outshines antiquity, its deeds surpass the virtue of old.

sentences.zh: 聖上天飛踐極，迄茲二十四載。

translations.literal: The Sage above, soaring to tread the summit, has reached this twenty-fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: The Sage-Emperor has ascended the throne and reigned these twenty-four years.

sentences.zh: 道化周流，玄澤汪濊。

translations.literal: The Way's transformation circulates everywhere; dark grace is vast and deep.
translations.idiomatic: The Way flows through all; profound grace spreads wide and deep.

sentences.zh: 地平天成，上下含熙；

translations.literal: Earth is level and Heaven's work complete; above and below hold radiance;
translations.idiomatic: Earth is level, Heaven's task fulfilled; above and below share its light;

sentences.zh: 文同軌通，表裏禔福。

translations.literal: writing shares the same track and paths connect; within and without receive blessing.
translations.idiomatic: culture unites the realm, roads run true; within and without, blessing rests.

sentences.zh: 耀德中區，黎庶知讓；

translations.literal: virtue shines in the central lands, the common people know yielding;
translations.idiomatic: Virtue radiates through the heartland, the people know modesty;

sentences.zh: 觀英遐表，夷貉懷惠。

translations.literal: beholding excellence in distant regions, barbarians and Mo hold kindness in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: gazing to distant borders, barbarians cherish his grace.

sentences.zh: 卹勤秩禮，罷露臺之金；

translations.literal: He pities toil and orders the rites, abolishing the gold for the Dew Terrace;
translations.idiomatic: He pities labor and sets rites in order, abolishing the gold for the Dew Terrace;

sentences.zh: 紓國振民，傾鉅橋之粟。

translations.literal: he eases the state and revives the people, pouring out the grain of the Great Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: he eases the realm and revives the people, pouring out the grain hoarded at Juliao.

sentences.zh: 約違迫脅，奢去泰甚。

translations.literal: He restrains what violates and compels by force, removing luxury and excess.
translations.idiomatic: He curbs coercion and extortion, stripping away extravagance and excess.

sentences.zh: 燕無留飲，畋不盤樂。

translations.literal: At banquets no lingering in drink; on hunts no unrestrained pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: At feasts he does not linger over wine; on the hunt he takes no unrestrained delight.

sentences.zh: 物色異人，優游據正。

translations.literal: He seeks out extraordinary men, at ease yet holding to the upright.
translations.idiomatic: He seeks out extraordinary men, at ease yet firm in righteousness.

sentences.zh: 顯不失心，幽無怨氣。

translations.literal: The manifest do not lose heart; the hidden harbor no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The eminent do not lose heart; the obscure harbor no grievance.

sentences.zh: 精炤日月，事洞天情。

translations.literal: His essence illumines sun and moon; his affairs penetrate Heaven's feelings.
translations.idiomatic: His spirit shines like sun and moon; his deeds accord with Heaven's intent.

sentences.zh: 故不勞杖斧之臣，號令不嚴而自肅；

translations.literal: Therefore without troubling ministers of axe and staff, his commands need no severity yet all are disciplined;
translations.idiomatic: Thus without relying on harsh ministers, his orders need no severity yet all are disciplined;

sentences.zh: 無辱鳳舉之使，靈怪不召而自彰。

translations.literal: without disgracing envoys who raise the phoenix, spirits and marvels need no summons yet manifest themselves.
translations.idiomatic: without sending envoys to seek omens, spirits and marvels appear unbidden.

sentences.zh: 萬里神行，飆塵不起。

translations.literal: For ten thousand li his spirit moves; whirlwind dust does not rise.
translations.idiomatic: His spirit ranges ten thousand li; no storm of dust arises.

sentences.zh: 農商野廬，邊城偃柝。

translations.literal: Farmers and merchants in wild huts; on the border walls the watch-clappers lie still.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers and merchants dwell in peace; on the frontier the watch-drums fall silent.

sentences.zh: 冀馬南金，填委內府；

translations.literal: Horses of Ji and southern gold fill and heap the inner treasury;
translations.idiomatic: Steeds of Ji and gold of the south overflow the inner treasury;

sentences.zh: 馴象西爵，充羅外囿。

translations.literal: tame elephants of the western tribute fill and spread through the outer parks.
translations.idiomatic: tame elephants from the western tribute fill the outer parks.

sentences.zh: 阿紈綦組之饒，衣覆宗國；

translations.literal: The abundance of fine silk and patterned ribbons clothes and covers the imperial clan;
translations.idiomatic: Fine silks and brocades clothe the imperial house;

sentences.zh: 漁鹽杞梓之利，傍贍荒遐。

translations.literal: the profit of fishing, salt, and catalpa timber supplies even the wild and remote.
translations.idiomatic: gain from fish, salt, and timber sustains even the farthest wilds.

sentences.zh: 士民殷富，五陵既有慚德；

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners are rich and full; the Five Mausoleums would already feel ashamed in virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and people are rich; the Five Mausoleums would blush at their virtue;

sentences.zh: 宮宇宏麗，三川莫之能比。

translations.literal: palaces and halls are grand and splendid—none of the Three Rivers can compare.
translations.idiomatic: palaces tower in splendor beyond anything the Three Rivers ever knew.

sentences.zh: 閭閈有盈，歌吹無絕。

translations.literal: Lanes and gates are full; songs and pipes never cease.
translations.idiomatic: Lanes overflow with life; song and music never cease.

sentences.zh: 朱輪疊轍，華冕重肩。

translations.literal: Vermilion wheels overlap in ruts; flower caps press shoulder to shoulder.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion wheels crowd the roads; noble hats press shoulder to shoulder.

sentences.zh: 豈徒世無窮人，民獲休息，朝呼韓、罷酤鐵而已哉！

translations.literal: Is it only that the age has no poor men, the people obtain rest, the court calls Han and abolishes the iron monopoly—that alone?
translations.idiomatic: Is this merely the age of no beggars, of rested people, of Han at court and the end of the iron monopoly?

sentences.zh: 是以嘉祥累仍，福應尤盛：青丘之狐，丹穴之鳥，棲阿閣，遊禁園。

translations.literal: Therefore auspicious signs come repeatedly, blessed responses especially abundant: the fox of Green Mound, the bird of Cinnabar Cave—roosting in the Epang Tower, wandering the forbidden gardens.
translations.idiomatic: Hence auspicious omens come again and again, blessings abound: the fox of Green Mound, the bird of Cinnabar Cave—roosting in the imperial tower, wandering the forbidden gardens.

sentences.zh: 金芝九莖，木禾六刃，秀銅池，發膏畝。

translations.literal: Golden fungus with nine stems, wooden grain with six ears—splendid in the Bronze Pool, sprouting in fertile fields.
translations.idiomatic: Golden fungus of nine stems, grain with six ears—blooming by the Bronze Pool, springing from fertile fields.

sentences.zh: 宜以協調律呂，謁薦郊廟，煙霏霧集，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Fit to harmonize pitch-pipes, to present offerings at the suburban altars—mist and fog gather in such numbers they cannot be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy to tune the pitch-pipes and offer at the suburban altars—omens gather like mist beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 然而聖上猶昧旦夙興，若有望而未至，閎規遠圖，如有追而莫及，神明之貺，推而弗居也。

translations.literal: Yet the Sage above still rises before dawn as if expecting what has not yet arrived, his vast plan and far design as if pursuing what he cannot overtake, the spirits' gifts—he pushes them away and does not occupy them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Sage-Emperor still rises before dawn as though awaiting what has not come, his grand design ever reaching beyond his grasp, the spirits' gifts—he declines them and will not rest upon them.

sentences.zh: 是以琬碑鏐檢，盛典蕪而不洽；

translations.literal: Therefore jade tablets and bronze inscriptions, great rites lie fallow and unfulfilled;
translations.idiomatic: Hence jade tablets and bronze inscriptions—the great rites lie neglected and unfulfilled;

sentences.zh: 朝神省方，大化抑而未許。

translations.literal: audiences with the spirits and inspection tours of the regions, the great transformation is held back and not granted.
translations.idiomatic: audiences with the spirits and tours of the realm—the great transformation is held back and not yet granted.

sentences.zh: 崇文協律之士，蘊儛頌於外；

translations.literal: men who honor letters and harmonize pitch-pipes harbor eulogies within;
translations.idiomatic: Men of letters who tune the pipes harbor songs of praise within;

sentences.zh: 坐朝陪宴之臣，懷揄揚於內，三靈佇眷，九壤注心，既有日矣。

translations.literal: ministers who sit at court and attend banquets hold praise in their hearts; the three spirits wait in regard, the nine realms fix their hearts—this has been so for days already.
translations.idiomatic: courtiers at audience and feast hold praise in their hearts; Heaven, Earth, and Man wait in longing, the nine realms fix their hearts—this has been so for many a day.

sentences.zh: 歲宮乾維，月躔蒼陸，長河巨濟，異源同清，澄波萬壑，潔瀾千里。

translations.literal: The year's palace in the Qian quadrant, the moon treading the azure land; the Long River and the Great Ji—different sources, one clarity; clear waves in ten thousand ravines, pure billows for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The year turns in the celestial palace, the moon crosses the azure land; the Long River and the Great Ji—different sources, one clarity; clear waves fill ten thousand valleys, pure currents run a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 斯誠曠世偉觀，昭啟皇明者也。

translations.literal: This is truly a vision spanning the ages, proclaiming and opening the imperial brightness.
translations.idiomatic: This is truly a sight unseen in ages, heralding the dynasty's radiant dawn.

sentences.zh: 語曰：「影從表，瑞從德。」

translations.literal: A saying runs: "Shadow follows the marker; auspicious signs follow virtue."
translations.idiomatic: The saying goes: "Shadow follows the gnomon; omens follow virtue."

sentences.zh: 此其效焉。

translations.literal: This is its effect.
translations.idiomatic: So it proves here.

sentences.zh: 宣尼稱「鳳鳥不至，河不出圖。」

translations.literal: Confucius said, "The phoenix bird does not come; the river does not yield the chart."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "The phoenix does not come; the river yields no chart."

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「俟河之清，人壽幾何！」

translations.literal: The Commentary says: "Wait for the river to clear—how many years is a man's life!"
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: "Wait for the river to clear—how long is a man's life!"

sentences.zh: 皆傷不可見也。

translations.literal: All grieve that these cannot be seen.
translations.idiomatic: All mourn what they could not live to see.

sentences.zh: 然則古人所不見者，今殫見之矣。

translations.literal: Thus what men of old did not see, today we fully see.
translations.idiomatic: What the ancients never saw, we now see in full.

sentences.zh: 孟軻曰：「千載一聖，是旦暮也。」

translations.literal: Meng Ke said: "A sage once in a thousand years—this is but morning and evening."
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said: "A sage once in a thousand years—this is but a single dawn and dusk."

sentences.zh: 豈不大哉。

translations.literal: How is this not great!
translations.idiomatic: How great is this!

sentences.zh: 夫四皇六帝，樹聲長世，大寶也。

translations.literal: The Four August Ones and Six Thearchs, planting fame for long ages—this is the great treasure.
translations.idiomatic: The Four August Ones and Six Thearchs, planting fame for ages—that is the great treasure.

sentences.zh: 澤浸群生，國富刑清，鴻德也。

translations.literal: Grace soaking the multitude, the state rich and punishments clear—this is vast virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Grace soaking all living things, the realm rich and punishments clear—that is vast virtue.

sentences.zh: 制禮裁樂，惇風遷俗，文教也。

translations.literal: Instituting rites and trimming music, thickening the wind and shifting custom—this is civil teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Instituting rites and shaping music, deepening custom and shifting the age—that is civil teaching.

sentences.zh: 誅華逋羯，束顙絳闕，武功也。

translations.literal: Punishing the splendor of fugitive Jie, binding foreheads at the crimson gate—this is martial achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing rebels and barbarians, binding captives at the crimson gate—that is martial achievement.

sentences.zh: 鳴鳥躍魚，滌穢河渠，至祥也。

translations.literal: Singing birds and leaping fish, cleansing filth from rivers and canals—this is utmost auspiciousness.
translations.idiomatic: Singing birds and leaping fish, cleansing the rivers and canals—that is the supreme omen.

sentences.zh: 大寶鴻德，文教武功，其崇如此；

translations.literal: Great treasure, vast virtue, civil teaching, martial achievement—their loftiness is thus;
translations.idiomatic: Great treasure, vast virtue, civil teaching, martial achievement—so lofty are these;

sentences.zh: 幽明協贊，民祇與能，厥應如彼。

translations.literal: dark and bright assist in praise, the people's spirits join in power—its responses are like those.
translations.idiomatic: dark and bright unite in praise, spirits and people join in power—such are its responses.

sentences.zh: 唯天為大，堯實則之；

translations.literal: Only Heaven is great—Yao in truth took it as his model;
translations.idiomatic: Only Heaven is great—and Yao took it as his model;

sentences.zh: 皇哉唐哉，疇與為讓。

translations.literal: How splendid is Tang! How splendid is Yu! With whom could he yield?
translations.idiomatic: How splendid is Tang! How splendid is Yu! Who could match him in yielding the throne?

sentences.zh: 抑又聞之，勢之所覃者淺，則美之所傳者近；

translations.literal: Moreover I have heard: where influence extends shallowly, what beauty is transmitted stays near;
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard: when influence spreads shallowly, fame travels only a short way;

sentences.zh: 道之所感者深，則慶之所流者遠。

translations.literal: where the Way moves one deeply, the blessings that flow reach far.
translations.idiomatic: when the Way touches one deeply, grace flows to distant ages.

sentences.zh: 是以豐功韙命，潤色縢策，盛德形容，藻被歌頌。

translations.literal: Therefore grand achievement and mandate most fair, embellishing and coloring the bamboo bundles; great virtue portrayed, adorned and covered with praise songs.
translations.idiomatic: Hence grand deeds and a glorious mandate adorn the bamboo chronicles; great virtue takes form, clothed in hymn and praise.

sentences.zh: 察之上代，則奚斯、吉甫之徒，鳴玉鑾於前；

translations.literal: Examining high antiquity, men like Xi Si and Ji Fu sounded jade tinkling at the fore;
translations.idiomatic: Looking to high antiquity, Xi Si and Ji Fu and their kind led the way with jade-mounted chariots;

sentences.zh: 視之中古，則相如、王褒之屬，施金羈於後。

translations.literal: viewing middle antiquity, men like Xiangru and Wang Bao and their sort placed golden bridles behind.
translations.idiomatic: in middle antiquity, Xiangru, Wang Bao, and their peers followed with golden bridles.

sentences.zh: 絕景揚光，清埃繼路，班固稱漢成之世，奏御者千有餘篇，文章之盛，與三代同風。

translations.literal: Peerless scenes raise light, clear dust follows on the road; Ban Gu praised the age of Han Cheng: memorials presented numbered more than a thousand—literary flowering then matched the Three Dynasties in wind.
translations.idiomatic: Their splendor outshines all before; fresh trails follow in the dust. Ban Gu wrote that in Chengdi's Han more than a thousand works were presented at court—letters at their peak, matching the Three Dynasties in spirit.

sentences.zh: 由是言之，斯乃臣子舊職，國家通義，不可輟也。

translations.literal: From this speaking, this is the old duty of ministers and sons, the universal righteousness of the state—it cannot be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In this lies the ancient duty of subjects and the state's enduring obligation—it must not cease.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不敏，寧不勉乎。

translations.literal: Though your servant is not keen, how could he not strive?
translations.idiomatic: Unworthy though I am, how could I fail to strive?

sentences.zh: 世祖以照為中書舍人。

translations.literal: The Shizu made Zhao Palace Secretary within the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu appointed Bao Zhao palace secretary.

sentences.zh: 上好為文章，自謂物莫能及，照悟其旨，為文多鄙言累句，當時咸謂照才盡，實不然也。

translations.literal: The sovereign loved composing literature and deemed nothing on earth his equal; Zhao grasped his intent and wrote much in vulgar words and piled clauses—at the time all said Zhao's talent was exhausted, which was in fact not so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved to write and thought nothing could match him; Bao Zhao understood and deliberately wrote in coarse, repetitive prose. The court then said his talent was spent—but that was not true.

sentences.zh: 臨海王子頊為荊州，照為前軍參軍，掌書記之任。

translations.literal: The Prince of Linhai, Zi, was made Governor of Jingzhou; Zhao was Forward Army Staff Officer, holding the post of secretary and recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zi of Linhai became governor of Jingzhou, Bao Zhao served as forward army staff officer in charge of secretarial work.

sentences.zh: 子頊敗，為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: When Zi was defeated, he was killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Zi was defeated, mutinous troops killed him.

sentences.zh: 子哀王燁字景舒嗣，官至通直郎，為元兇所殺。

translations.literal: His son, King Ai Ye, courtesy name Jingshu, succeeded; he reached the post of Unimpeded Gentleman and was killed by the Arch-Culprit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ye, King Ai, styled Jingshu, succeeded him, rose to unimpeded gentleman, and was killed by the Arch-Culprit Liu Shao.

sentences.zh: 追贈散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 子綽，字子流嗣，官至步兵校尉。

translations.literal: His son Chuo, courtesy name Ziliu, succeeded; he reached the post of Footsoldier Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chuo, styled Ziliu, succeeded and rose to footsoldier commandant.

sentences.zh: 昇明三年反，伏誅，國除。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengming he rebelled, was executed, and the state was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 3 he rebelled, was executed, and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 綽弟綰，早卒。

translations.literal: Chuo's younger brother Wan died young.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo's younger brother Wan died young.

sentences.zh: 燁弟衍，太子舍人。

translations.literal: Ye's younger brother Yan was an Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's younger brother Yan was attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 衍弟鏡，宣城太守。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Jing was Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Jing was administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 鏡弟穎，前將軍。

translations.literal: Jing's younger brother Ying was General of the Van.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's younger brother Ying was general of the van.

sentences.zh: 穎弟倩，南新蔡太守。

translations.literal: Ying's younger brother Qian was Administrator of Southern Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's younger brother Qian was administrator of Southern Xincai.

sentences.zh: 遵考，高祖族弟也。

translations.literal: Zunkao was a clan cousin of the Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Zunkao was a cousin of the Founder within the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖淳，皇曾祖武原令混之弟，官至正員郎。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Chun was the younger brother of Hun, the imperial great-great-grandfather who had been Magistrate of Wuyuan; he himself reached the post of Regular Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Chun was younger brother to Hun, the Founder's great-grandfather who had served as magistrate of Wuyuan; Chun himself reached regular gentleman.

sentences.zh: 祖巗，海西令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan was Magistrate of Haixi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan was magistrate of Haixi.

sentences.zh: 父涓子，彭城內史。

translations.literal: His father Juanzi was Interior Minister of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Juanzi was interior minister of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 遵考始為將軍振武參軍，預討盧循，封鄉侯。

translations.literal: Zunkao first served as Staff Officer under the General Who Quells Martial Might, took part in the campaign against Lu Xun, and was enfeoffed as a district marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Zunkao first served as staff officer to the General Who Quells Martial Might, joined the campaign against Lu Xun, and was enfeoffed as district marquis.

sentences.zh: 自建威將軍、彭城內史隨高祖北伐。

translations.literal: From the post of General Who Establishes Martial Might and Interior Minister of Pengcheng he followed the Gaozu on the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: As general who establishes martial might and interior minister of Pengcheng, he followed the Founder on the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 時高祖諸子竝弱，宗室唯有遵考。

translations.literal: At that time all the Gaozu's sons were still young; of the imperial clan only Zunkao stood forth.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder's sons were still young; of the imperial clan only Zunkao was grown.

sentences.zh: 長安平定，以督并州、司州之北河東、北平陽、北雍州之新平、安定五郡諸軍事、輔國將軍、并州刺史，領河東太守，鎮蒲阪。

translations.literal: When Chang'an was pacified, he was made to oversee military affairs of the five commanderies of Northern Hedong and Northern Pingyang in Bing and Si, and Xinping and Anding in Northern Yong, as General Who Assists the State, Inspector of Bingzhou, concurrently Administrator of Hedong, garrisoning Puban.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang'an was pacified, he was appointed to oversee military affairs in five commanderies across Bing, Si, and Northern Yong, made general who assists the state and inspector of Bing, with concurrent duties as administrator of Hedong, garrisoning Puban.

sentences.zh: 關中失守，南還，除游擊將軍，遷冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Guanzhong was lost he returned south; he was relieved as General Who Storms Forth and was promoted to General Who Champions the State.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanzhong fell he marched south; he was made general who storms forth, then promoted to general who champions the state.

sentences.zh: 晉帝遜位居秣陵宮，遵考領兵防衛。

translations.literal: When the Jin emperor abdicated and dwelt at the Moling Palace, Zunkao commanded troops to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin emperor abdicated to the Moling palace, Zunkao led troops to guard him.

sentences.zh: 高祖初即大位，下推恩之詔，曰：「遵考服屬之親，國戚未遠，宗室無多，宜蒙寵爵。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu first took the great throne, he issued an edict extending grace, saying: "Zunkao is kin within the mourning grades; his imperial affinity is not distant; the imperial clan is not numerous—he should receive ennobled rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder first took the throne, he issued a grace edict: "Zunkao is close kin in mourning degree, near in imperial affinity; the clan is small—he should receive a noble fief.

sentences.zh: 可封營浦縣侯，食邑五百戶。」

translations.literal: He may be enfeoffed as Marquis of Yingpu County with a fief of five hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be enfeoffed as Marquis of Yingpu with five hundred households."

sentences.zh: 以本號為彭城、沛二郡太守。

translations.literal: With his existing title he served concurrently as Governor of the two commanderies of Pengcheng and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his existing rank and concurrently governed Pengcheng and Pe commanderies.

sentences.zh: 景平元年，遷右衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingping he was transferred to General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingping 1 he was made general of the right guard.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二年，出為征虜將軍、淮南太守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanjia he went out as General Who Captures Barbarians and Administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanjia he left the capital as general who captures barbarians and administrator of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉使持節，領護軍，入直殿省。

translations.literal: The next year he was made Credential Bearer and concurrently Colonel of the Guard Army, entering to attend in the Hall Department.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he received the credential staff, became colonel of the guard army, and attended within the palace offices.

sentences.zh: 出為使持節、督雍、梁、南北秦四州、荊州之南陽、竟陵、順陽、襄陽、新野、隨六郡諸軍事、征虜將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史，襄陽、新野二郡太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Credential Bearer, overseeing military affairs in the four provinces of Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, and Southern Qin and the six commanderies of Nanyang, Jingling, Shunyang, Xiangyang, Xinye, and Sui in Jingzhou, as General Who Captures Barbarians, Colonel Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and Inspector of Yongzhou, concurrently Governor of the two commanderies of Xiangyang and Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as credential bearer to command Yong, Liang, and Northern and Southern Qin and six Jing commanderies, as general who captures barbarians, colonel who pacifies the barbarians, and inspector of Yong, concurrently governing Xiangyang and Xinye.

sentences.zh: 遵考為政嚴暴，聚斂無節。

translations.literal: Zunkao's governance was severe and violent; he gathered taxes without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Zunkao governed with harsh cruelty and extorted without limit.

sentences.zh: 五年，為有司所糾，上不問，赦還都。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was impeached by the relevant offices; the sovereign did not inquire and pardoned him to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 the censorate impeached him; the emperor took no action and pardoned him back to court.

sentences.zh: 七年，除太子右衛率，加給事中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was relieved as Colonel of the Right Guard for the Heir Apparent and made Honorary Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was made colonel of the right guard for the heir apparent with honorary attendant status.

sentences.zh: 明年，督南徐、兗州之江北、淮南諸軍事、征虜將軍、南兗州刺史，領廣陵太守。

translations.literal: The next year he oversaw military affairs in Jiangbei and Huainan in Southern Xu and Yanzhou, as General Who Captures Barbarians and Inspector of Southern Yanzhou, concurrently Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he commanded Jiangbei and Huainan in Southern Xu and Yan as general who captures barbarians and inspector of Southern Yan, concurrently administering Guangling.

sentences.zh: 又徵為侍中，領後軍將軍，徙太常。

translations.literal: Again he was summoned as Palace Attendant, concurrently General of the Rear Army, and transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as palace attendant and general of the rear army, then made minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷右衛將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to General of the Right Guard and made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he became general of the right guard and regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 十二年，坐厲疾不待對，免常侍，以侯領右衛。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, because he feigned serious illness and would not await audience, he was removed from regular attendant; as marquis he held the right guard.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he feigned grave illness and refused audience; he lost regular attendant rank but kept the right guard as marquis.

sentences.zh: 明年，復本官。

translations.literal: The next year he recovered his former office.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he regained his former post.

sentences.zh: 十五年，又領徐州大中正、太子中庶子，本官如故。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he also held Senior Rectifier of Xuzhou and Senior Attendant of the Heir Apparent; his original offices remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he also held senior rectifier of Xuzhou and senior attendant of the heir apparent, retaining his other titles.

sentences.zh: 其年，監徐、兗二州、豫州之梁郡諸軍事、前將軍、徐、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: That same year he oversaw military affairs in the two provinces of Xu and Yan and Liang commandery in Yuzhou, as General of the Van and Inspector of the two provinces of Xu and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: That year he oversaw Xu and Yan and Liang commandery in Yu as general of the van and inspector of Xu and Yan.

sentences.zh: 未之鎮，留為侍中，領左衛將軍。

translations.literal: Before going to the garrison he was retained as Palace Attendant, concurrently General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before taking up his post he was kept at court as palace attendant and general of the left guard.

sentences.zh: 明年，出為使持節、監豫、司、雍、并四州、南豫州之梁郡、弋陽、馬頭、荊州之義陽四郡諸軍事、前將軍、豫州刺史，領南梁郡太守。

translations.literal: The next year he went out as Credential Bearer, overseeing military affairs in the four provinces of Yu, Si, Yong, and Bing and the four commanderies of Liang, Yiyang, Matou, and Yiyang in Southern Yu and Jing, as General of the Van and Inspector of Yuzhou, concurrently Administrator of Southern Liang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he went out as credential bearer to oversee Yu, Si, Yong, and Bing and four border commanderies, as general of the van and inspector of Yu, concurrently administering Southern Liang.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，坐統內旱，百姓饑，詔加賑給，而遵考不奉符旨，免官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, because of drought within his command and the people starving, an edict ordered added relief—but Zunkao did not follow the credential's intent and was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 a drought in his province brought famine; though ordered to provide relief Zunkao ignored the edict and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 起為散騎常侍、五兵尚書，遷吳興太守，秩中二千石。

translations.literal: He was raised as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Minister of the Five Troops, transferred to Administrator of Wuxing with stipend of two thousand dan.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed regular attendant and minister of the five troops, then made administrator of Wuxing at two thousand-dan rank.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，徵為領軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was summoned as Colonel Director of Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 he was summoned as colonel director of retainers.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，索虜南至瓜步，率軍出江上，假節蓋。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year the Northern Wei came south to Guabu; he led troops out onto the river and was given the ceremonial credential staff and canopy.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 the Northern Wei reached Guabu; he led troops onto the Yangzi with ceremonial staff and canopy.

sentences.zh: 三十年，復出為使持節，監豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he again went out with credential staff as overseer of the Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 30 he again went out as credential bearer overseeing Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 元兇弑立，進號安西將軍，遣外監徐安期、仰捷祖防守之。

translations.literal: When the Arch-Culprit usurped the throne he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West and sent the outer supervisors Xu Anqi and Yang Jiezu to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Arch-Culprit seized the throne he was promoted to general who pacifies the west; the outer supervisors Xu Anqi and Yang Jiezu were sent to guard him.

sentences.zh: 遵考斬安期等，起義兵應南譙王義宣，義宣加遵考鎮西將軍。

translations.literal: Zunkao beheaded Anqi and the others, raised righteous troops in response to Prince Yixuan of Southern Qiao, and Yixuan advanced Zunkao to General Who Garrisons the West.
translations.idiomatic: Zunkao executed Anqi and the others, raised forces for Prince Yixuan of Southern Qiao, who promoted him to general who garrisons the west.

sentences.zh: 夏侯獻率眾至瓜步承候世祖，又坐免官。

translations.literal: Xiahou Xian led troops to Guabu to await the Shizu and again was removed from office for this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Xian marched to Guabu to receive Emperor Xiaowu and Zunkao was again dismissed for it.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年，魯爽、臧質反，起為征虜將軍，率眾屯臨沂縣，仍除吳興太守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaojian, Lu Shuang and Zang Zhi rebelled; he was raised as General Who Captures Barbarians, led troops to encamp at Linyi County, and was concurrently made Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 1, when Lu Shuang and Zang Zhi rebelled, he was raised as general who captures barbarians, encamped at Linyi, and made administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 明年，徵為湘州刺史，未行，遷尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned as Inspector of Xiangzhou; before departing he was transferred to Left Vice-Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was summoned as inspector of Xiangzhou but, before leaving, was made left vice-director.

sentences.zh: 三年，轉丹陽尹，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Governor of Danyang and made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he became governor of Danyang and regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 復為尚書右僕射，領太子右衛率。

translations.literal: Again he was made Right Vice-Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Colonel of the Right Guard for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made right vice-director and colonel of the right guard for the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 明年，又除領軍將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: The next year he was again relieved as Colonel Director of Retainers and made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was again colonel director of retainers with regular attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 五年，復遷尚書右僕射、金紫光祿大夫，常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was again transferred to Right Vice-Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; his regular attendant post remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he returned as right vice-director and grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon, keeping regular attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉左僕射，常侍如故。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Left Vice-Director; his regular attendant post remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became left vice-director, retaining regular attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 又領徐州刺史、大中正、崇憲太僕。

translations.literal: He also held Inspector of Xuzhou, Senior Rectifier, and Honorary Grand Minister of Splendid Felicity.
translations.idiomatic: He also held inspector of Xuzhou, senior rectifier, and honorary grand minister of splendid felicity.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝即位，遷特進、右光祿大夫，常侍、太僕如故。

translations.literal: When the Former Deposed Emperor took the throne he was promoted to Special Grand Master and Right Grand Master of Splendid Felicity; his regular attendant and grand minister posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Former Deposed Emperor took the throne he was made special grand master and right grand master of splendid felicity, keeping his attendant and grand minister posts.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，出督南豫州諸軍事、安西將軍、南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe he went out to oversee military affairs of Southern Yuzhou, as General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinghe 1 he went out to command Southern Yuzhou as general who pacifies the west and inspector.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，以為侍中、特進、右光祿大夫，領崇憲太僕，給親侍三十人。

translations.literal: When the Taizong took the throne he was made Palace Attendant, Special Grand Master, and Right Grand Master of Splendid Felicity, concurrently Honorary Grand Minister of Splendid Felicity, with thirty personal attendants granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne he was made palace attendant, special grand master, and right grand master of splendid felicity, with concurrent grand minister of splendid felicity and thirty personal attendants.

sentences.zh: 崇憲太后崩，太僕解，餘如故。

translations.literal: When Honored Dowager Chongxian died, he was relieved of grand minister; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Honored Dowager Chongxian died he relinquished grand minister but kept his other titles.

sentences.zh: 泰始五年，賜几杖，大官四時賜珍味，疾病太醫給藥，固辭几杖。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taishi he was granted couch and staff; the Imperial Kitchen sent delicacies through the four seasons; when ill the Imperial Physicians supplied medicine—he firmly declined couch and staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taishi he was granted couch and staff, seasonal delicacies from the imperial kitchen, and imperial physicians when ill—he firmly declined the couch and staff.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝即位，進左光祿大夫，餘如故。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne he was advanced to Left Grand Master of Splendid Felicity; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne he was promoted to left grand master of splendid felicity, keeping his other titles.

sentences.zh: 元徽元年卒，時年八十二。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhui he died, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yuanhui 1, aged eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 追贈左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，侍中如故。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Left Grand Master of Splendid Felicity and Keeper of the Gate with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies; his palace attendant post remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made left grand master of splendid felicity and keeper of the gate with three-excellencies credentials, keeping palace attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 諡曰元公。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Duke Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Duke Yuan.

sentences.zh: 遵考無才能，直以宗室不遠，故歷朝顯遇。

translations.literal: Zunkao had no talent or ability; solely because his imperial clan standing was not distant he received distinguished favor through successive reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Zunkao had no ability; only because he was not far removed in the clan did he enjoy conspicuous favor reign after reign.

sentences.zh: 年老有疾失明。

translations.literal: In old age he had illness and lost his sight.
translations.idiomatic: In old age illness left him blind.

sentences.zh: 子澄之，順帝昇明末貴達。

translations.literal: His son Chengzhi, toward the end of the Shengming era under Emperor Shun, reached high honor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengzhi rose to high honor at the end of the Shengming era under Emperor Shun.

sentences.zh: 澄之弟琨之，為竟陵王誕司空主簿。

translations.literal: Chengzhī's younger brother Kunzhi was Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works for Prince Dan of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhī's younger brother Kunzhi was chief clerk to the minister of works under Prince Dan of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 誕作亂，以為中兵參軍，不就，縶繫數十日，終不受，乃殺之。

translations.literal: When Dan rebelled he was appointed Middle Army Staff Officer but would not accept; he was bound and imprisoned for several tens of days, in the end would not submit, and was therefore killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan rebelled he was offered a middle army staff post but refused; bound and imprisoned for weeks, he still would not yield, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 追贈黃門郎。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made gentleman at the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 詔吏部尚書謝莊為之誄。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Xie Zhuang to compose his eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Minister of Personnel Xie Zhuang to compose his dirge.

sentences.zh: 遵考從弟思考，亦被遇。

translations.literal: Zunkao's younger cousin Sicai also received favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zunkao's cousin Sicai was also favored.

sentences.zh: 歷朝官，極清顯，為豫章、會稽太守，益、徐州刺史，凡經十郡三州。

translations.literal: He held office through successive reigns, reaching the utmost in pure distinction; he was Administrator of Yuzhang and Kuaiji, Inspector of Yi and Xu, and in all passed through ten commanderies and three provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He served through many reigns at the highest ranks, governing Yuzhang and Kuaiji and inspecting Yi and Xu—ten commanderies and three provinces in all.

sentences.zh: 泰始元年，卒於散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，時年七十五。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taishi he died while Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Taishi while regular attendant and grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon, aged seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 追贈特進，常侍，光祿如故。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Special Grand Master; his regular attendant and grand master posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made special grand master, retaining his attendant and splendid felicity titles.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：餘妖內侮，偏眾西臨，荀、桓交逼，荊楚之勢危矣。

translations.literal: The Historian says: With remnant demons invading within and partial hosts pressing from the west, Xun and Huan pressing on both sides, the situation in Jing and Chu was perilous indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The Historian says: With remnant rebels within and enemy columns on the west, Xun and Huan pressing from every side, Jing and Chu stood in grave peril.

sentences.zh: 必使上略未盡，一筭或遺，則城壞壓境，上流之難方結。

translations.literal: Had the supreme strategy not been fully deployed and a single calculation been missed, then walls would collapse pressing the borderlands and difficulty on the upper reaches would just be knitting together.
translations.idiomatic: Had the grand design fallen short by even one move, the frontier would have collapsed and the upper Yangzi trap would have closed.

sentences.zh: 敵資三分有二之形，北向而爭天下，則我全勝之道，或未可知。

translations.literal: The enemy would have had the form of possessing two thirds; turning north to contend for All under Heaven, then our path to complete victory might or might not have been known.
translations.idiomatic: The foe would have held two thirds of the realm and turned north to seize the empire—and our path to total victory might never have been known.

sentences.zh: 烈武王覽群才，揚盛策，一舉磔勍寇，非曰天時，抑亦人謀也。

translations.literal: Prince Lie Wu surveyed the host of talents, raised a grand plan, and in one stroke executed the fierce enemy band—this is not called Heaven's season; it is rather human design.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lie Wu gathered talent, raised a bold design, and in one stroke destroyed the fierce foe—not mere heaven's favor, but human counsel at work.

sentences.zh: 降年不永，遂不得與大業始終，惜矣哉！

translations.literal: Heaven granted him few years; thus he could not see the great enterprise through to the end—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven gave him few years, and he could not see the great enterprise through to its end—alas!
